literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 启用 SAM 的 SEM 揭示了 H3N2 病毒颗粒表面明显的“波状”形貌图案,这被解释为临界点干燥收缩导致的制剂诱导伪影。超高压电子断层扫描证实,含有尖峰的包膜结构有助于观察到这种形态。SAM 与负染色的兼容性允许通过不同的包膜变形直接观察乙醇诱导的 H3N2 病毒灭活。 [10.1093/jmicro/dfag042]
结果体内评估表明,猪对人 H1 疫苗 候选药物在所有三种 HA 抗原上诱导了最广泛的体液 IgG 反应,而台湾猪 H1 候选药物则引发了最窄的交叉反应免疫。 [10.1186/s12917-026-06097-0]
仅在 2025-2026 年季节,流感亚型与第 28 天 死亡率 的显着风险无关。在 40 名 甲型H3N2流感病毒 感染者中,33 人(82.5%)属于 K 亚支。系统发育分析显示,没有根据严重程度进行聚类。 [10.1093/cid/ciag648]
更正报告称,原始文章缺少有关致谢部分的信息,其中包括有关研究所用平台和财务支持的详细信息。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014784]
与对照溶液相比,两种含有粘蛋白的基质都限制了病毒的通过。病毒 RNA 转移和保留感染性因基质和病毒而异,但在任一基质内均未检测到 H1N1pdm 和 H5N1 之间存在统计学上的显着差异。 [10.1038/s44298-026-00257-7]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical 'wavy' pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact from critical point drying shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. [10.1093/jmicro/dfag042]

Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%). [10.1186/s12879-026-14841-y]

Results In vivo evaluation demonstrated that the swine-to-human H1 vaccine candidate induced the broadest humoral IgG response across all three HA antigens, whereas the Taiwan porcine H1 candidate elicited the narrowest cross-reactive immunity. [10.1186/s12917-026-06097-0]

In the 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. Phylogenetic analyses showed no clustering according to severity. [10.1093/cid/ciag648]

The correction reports that the original article was missing information about the Acknowledgement section, which includes details on the platforms and financial support used for the research. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014784]

news.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 该报告指出,流感活动有所增加,且在低水平传播,流感样疾病的急诊部门就诊人数超过季节性预期水平。同时,报告还提到流感确诊的急性呼吸道感染病例数较前一周有所上升。 [news-197ad873751ae63d]
一项观察性研究调查了2023年11月至2024年12月期间在伊朗设拉子住院患者中的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 分离株,揭示了基因组变异但未发现主要抗病毒药物耐药性(N1)。 [news-688bfc4aa33ec953]
全国流感检测阳性率超过10%,主要流行的病毒为流感A型(甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09和甲型H3N2流感病毒)以及流感B型(Victoria和Yamagata谱系)。CDC报告称流感活动和住院病例增加,初步评估显示病情较轻。 [news-e0a1534ead7eb995]
文章报道了孕期流感的风险,包括严重症状、并发症以及疫苗接种和及时就医的重要性。 [news-a639bff5ac302078]
季节性流感感染会增加心脏病发作和中风的风险,如越南热带病国家医院和巴莫医院心血管研究所专家所报告。 [news-19060e437e8ac131]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Seasonal influenza viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: The report indicates that influenza activity increased and is circulating at low levels, with ED attendances for influenza-like-illness above seasonally expected levels. It also notes that influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection incidents increased compared with the previous week. [news-197ad873751ae63d]

An observational study investigated influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, between November 2023 and December 2024, revealing genomic variability but no major antiviral resistance mutations (N1). [news-688bfc4aa33ec953]

Flu test positivity exceeded 10% nationally, with influenza A (H1N1pdm09 and H3N2) and influenza B (Victoria and Yamagata lineages) being the dominant viruses. The CDC reported increased activity and hospitalizations, with a preliminary assessment of low severity. [news-e0a1534ead7eb995]
The article reports on the risks of influenza during pregnancy, including severe symptoms, complications, and the importance of vaccination and medical attention. [news-a639bff5ac302078]

Contracting seasonal flu increases the risk of heart attack and stroke, as reported by experts at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases and the Cardiovascular Institute, Bach Mai Hospital. [news-19060e437e8ac131]

papers.title: Penetration of avian and human influenza A viruses through mucus gel networks in vitro.
papers.abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a public-health concern because of their continuous evolution and zoonotic transmission. Respiratory mucus is the first extracellular barrier encountered by inhaled viruses, yet standardized approaches for studying influenza virus passage through mucus and the infectivity of transferred virus populations remain limited. Here, we established an in vitro virus–mucus penetration assay to analyze IAV interactions with standardized mucin-containing matrices. We used mucus from human Calu-3 airway epithelial cells cultured under air–liquid interface conditions and bovine submaxillary mucin as surrogate matrices. Preparations were normalized by total protein and characterized using biochemical and biophysical methods. We compared a human seasonal H1N1pdm virus with a highly-pathogenic avian H5N1 virus. Viral genome transfer was quantified by RT-qPCR, while retained infectivity was assessed in susceptible cells. Both mucin-containing matrices restricted viral passage compared with control solutions. Viral RNA transfer and retained infectivity varied by matrix and virus, although no statistically significant difference between H1N1pdm and H5N1 was detected within either matrix. Together, these results establish a framework integrating mucus characterization with complementary measurements of viral transfer and infectivity. This approach provides a basis for investigating influenza virus–mucus interactions under controlled conditions and can be extended to other IAV strains and physiologically relevant mucus sources.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a public-health concern because of their continuous evolution and zoonotic transmission. Respiratory mucus is the first extracellular barrier encountered by inhaled viruses, yet standardized approaches for studying influenza virus passage through mucus and the infectivity of transferred virus populations remain limited. Here, we established an in vitro virus–mucus penetration assay to analyze IAV interactions with standardized mucin-containing matrices. We used mucus from human Calu-3 airway epithelial cells cultured under air–liquid interface conditions and bovine submaxillary mucin as surrogate matrices. Preparations were normalized by total protein and characterized using biochemical and biophysical methods. We compared a human seasonal H1N1pdm virus with a highly-pathogenic avian H5N1 virus. This approach provides a basis for investigating influenza virus–mucus interactions under controlled conditions and can be extended to other IAV strains and physiologically relevant mucus sources.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为改进的 监测 和流感病毒诊断方法的开发提供信息,并指导通过粘液针对病毒 传播 的干预措施的设计。

papers.title: People With Influenza Requiring ICU Admission During the 2025-2026 Season, Marked by the Emergence of Influenza A(H3N2) Subclade K: A French Prospective Nationwide Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intense influenza activity has been reported alongside the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. While epidemiological studies have reported heterogeneous findings regarding public health impact, data remain lacking on its impact on clinical phenotype of people requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, observational SEVARVIR cohort study including people admitted in 42 French ICUs with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Primary end point was day-28 mortality. RESULTS: Seven hundred twenty-six people were admitted for influenza in 2024-2025 (n = 360) and 2025-2026 (n = 366). In 2025-2026, influenza subtype was available for 265 people; 49% (n = 129) had A(H1N1)pdm09 and 51% (n = 136) had A(H3N2) subtype infection. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection for whom whole-genome sequencing was available, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. In multivariable Cox analysis of the 2025-2026 season, age (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09]; P = .015), Clinical Frailty Scale (aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98]; P < .001), and sequential organ failure assessment score (aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26]; P = .003) were associated with an increased risk of death. In the 2024-2025/2025-2026 seasons or 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Phylogenetic analyses from our ICU cohort together with 600 contextual sequences from community-acquired influenza cases collected during the period showed no clustering according to severity. CONCLUSIONS: There was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill people with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05162508.

METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, observational SEVARVIR cohort study including people admitted in 42 French ICUs with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Primary end point was day-28 mortality. RESULTS: Seven hundred twenty-six people were admitted for influenza in 2024-2025 (n = 360) and 2025-2026 (n = 366). In 2025-2026, influenza subtype was available for 265 people; 49% (n = 129) had A(H1N1)pdm09 and 51% (n = 136) had A(H3N2) subtype infection. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection for whom whole-genome sequencing was available, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. In multivariable Cox analysis of the 2025-2026 season, age (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09]; P = .015), Clinical Frailty Scale (aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98]; P < .001), and sequential organ failure assessment score (aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26]; P = .003) were associated with an increased risk of death. In the 2024-2025/2025-2026 seasons or 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Phylogenetic analyses from our ICU cohort together with 600 contextual sequences from community-acquired influenza cases collected during the period showed no clustering according to severity. CONCLUSIONS: There was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill people with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05162508.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K on the clinical outcomes of people requiring ICU admission during the 2025-2026 influenza season. A prospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in 42 French ICUs, including 726 patients with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection. The primary endpoint was day-28 mortality, and whole-genome sequencing was performed on 40 patients with A(H3N2) infection. Results showed that influenza subtype was not significantly associated with day-28 mortality in the 2025-2026 season, and among those with A(H3N2) infection, 82.5% belonged to subclade K. The authors concluded that there was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill patients with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of subclade K. The study's observational design and lack of a control group limit the strength of the evidence, but the use of genomic data enhances its reliability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 据报道,随着流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 亚支的出现,流感活动也随之加剧。该研究旨在调查其对需要入住 ICU 的患者临床表型的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性、多中心、观察性 SEVARVIR 队列研究 研究在 42 个法国 ICU 中进行,其中包括 2024-2025 年和 2025-2026 年季节期间因实验室确诊流感感染入院的患者。总计726人,其中2024-2025赛季360人,2025-2026赛季366人。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,尽管出现了流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 K 分支,但没有证据表明 2025-2026 年季节期间流感重症患者的死亡风险增加。这一发现很新颖,因为它直接解决了 K 分支对 ICU 结局的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,流感甲型H3N2流感病毒 K亚支的出现并没有显着影响危重患者的死亡率率,这可能为未来的监测和季节性流感的公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,不包括对照组,这可能会限制证据的强度。然而,全 基因组 测序和系统发育分析的使用提供了一种稳健的方法学方法。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在流感甲型H3N2流感病毒亚系K出现的同时,报告了强烈的流感活动。尽管流行病学研究在公共卫生影响方面报告了异质性结果,但关于其对需要重症监护病房(ICU)入院人群临床表型的影响的数据仍然缺乏。方法:一项前瞻性、多中心、观察性SEVARVIR 队列研究研究,包括在2024-2025和2025-2026季节期间在42个法国ICU中接受实验室确诊流感感染的患者。主要终点是第28天死亡率。结果:在2024-2025年(n = 360)和2025-2026年(n = 366)期间,共有726名患者因流感入院。在2025-2026年,有265名患者的流感亚型可供分析;其中49%(n = 129)为甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09亚型感染,51%(n = 136)为甲型H3N2流感病毒亚型感染。在40名接受全基因组测序的甲型H3N2流感病毒感染患者中,33名(82.5%)属于亚系K。在2025-2026年季节的多变量Cox分析中,年龄(调整后风险比,aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09];P = .015)、临床脆弱性量表(aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98];P < .001)以及序贯器官衰竭评估评分(aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26];P = .003)与死亡风险增加相关。在2024-2025/2025-2026年季节或仅2025-2026年季节中,流感亚型与第28天死亡率的显著风险无关联。我们的ICU 队列研究的系统发育分析,结合了600个来自同期社区获得性流感病例的上下文序列,未显示根据严重程度的聚集。结论:在2025-2026年季节,尽管出现了流感甲型H3N2流感病毒亚系K,但没有证据表明重症流感患者死亡风险增加。试验注册号:NCT05162508。

papers.title: Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM): Ultracentrifugation-Free Electron Microscopy of Influenza A virus (H3N2) Morphology and Disinfectant-Induced Changes.
papers.abstract: Abstract Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal EM (SEM, TEM, STEM) visualization of progeny virus particles without prior concentration. SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical "wavy" pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, which is interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact arising from critical point drying (CPD) shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. Thus, SAM-facilitated SEM offers wide-field morphological insights complementing TEM's high-resolution internal structural analysis. Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. Furthermore, SAM's compatibility with negative staining allowed direct visualization of ethanol-induced H3N2 virus inactivation via distinct envelope deformations such as disruption and roughening. This feature makes SAM a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays. In conclusion, SAM provides a simple, rapid, artifact-mitigating approach for detailed morphological studies of H3N2 virus and antiviral agent evaluation, opening new perspectives in virological EM.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发一种方法来克服甲型流感病毒(H3N2)电子显微镜中超速离心引起的结构伪影,这是解决病毒超微结构的关键问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用电子显微镜技术(包括 SEM、TEM 和 STEM)设计并验证了甲型流感病毒 (H3N2) 可视化的基质粘附方法 (SAM)。
elements_zh.methods: SAM 通过利用 H3N2 病毒颗粒在感染过程中与细胞培养基质的自然粘附,绕过超速离心,无需事先浓缩即可实现有效的多模式 EM 可视化。
elements_zh.main_results: 启用 SAM 的 SEM 揭示了 H3N2 病毒颗粒表面明显的“波状”形貌图案,这被解释为临界点干燥收缩导致的制剂诱导伪影。超高压电子断层扫描证实,含有尖峰的包膜结构有助于观察到这种形态。SAM 与负染色的兼容性允许通过不同的包膜变形直接观察乙醇诱导的 H3N2 病毒灭活。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: SAM 为 H3N2 病毒的详细形态学研究和 抗病毒药物 制剂评估提供了一种简单、快速、减少伪影的方法,提供了广泛的形态学见解,补充了 TEM 的高分辨率内部结构分析。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: SAM 是一种有价值的工具,可用于直接形态学评估消毒剂功效、补充感染性测定并开辟病毒学 EM 的新视角。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 受感染细胞显着增强了病毒颗粒通过 SAM 与基质的粘附,表明细胞相关因子在这种固定中发挥着关键作用。然而,该研究并未报告 SAM 对其他流感病毒亚型或物种的普遍性。

papers.title_zh: 基质粘附法 (SAM):甲型流感病毒 (H3N2) 形态和消毒剂引起的变化的无超速离心电子显微镜。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal EM (SEM, TEM, STEM) visualization of progeny virus particles without prior concentration. SAM-enabled SEM revealed a distinct topographical "wavy" pattern on H3N2 virus particle surfaces, which is interpreted as a preparation-induced artifact arising from critical point drying (CPD) shrinkage. Ultra-high-voltage electron tomography confirmed that spike-containing envelope structures contribute to this observed morphology. Thus, SAM-facilitated SEM offers wide-field morphological insights complementing TEM's high-resolution internal structural analysis. Virus particle adhesion to the substrate via SAM was significantly enhanced by infected cells, suggesting a key role for cell-associated factors in this immobilization. Furthermore, SAM's compatibility with negative staining allowed direct visualization of ethanol-induced H3N2 virus inactivation via distinct envelope deformations such as disruption and roughening. This feature makes SAM a valuable tool for direct morphological assessment of disinfectant efficacy, complementing infectivity assays. In conclusion, SAM provides a simple, rapid, artifact-mitigating approach for detailed morphological studies of H3N2 virus and antiviral agent evaluation, opening new perspectives in virological EM.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 电子显微镜 (EM) 对于解析病毒超微结构至关重要,但用于样品浓缩的传统超速离心可能会导致结构伪影,特别是在甲型流感病毒等包膜病毒中。为了克服这个问题,我们开发并验证了基材粘附方法 (SAM)。这种简单的技术利用甲型流感病毒 (H3N2) 在感染过程中对细胞培养基质的自然粘附,绕过超速离心,无需事先浓缩即可对子代病毒颗粒进行有效的多模式 EM(SEM、TEM、STEM)可视化。启用 SAM 的 SEM 揭示了 H3N2 病毒颗粒表面明显的地形“波状”图案,这被解释为由临界点干燥 (CPD) 收缩引起的制剂诱导伪影。超高压电子断层扫描证实,含有尖峰的包膜结构有助于观察到这种形态。因此,SAM 辅助的 SEM 提供了宽视场形态学见解,补充了 TEM 的高分辨率内部结构分析。受感染细胞显着增强了病毒颗粒通过 SAM 与基质的粘附,表明细胞相关因子在这种固定中发挥着关键作用。此外,SAM 与负染色的兼容性允许通过不同的包膜变形(例如破坏和粗糙化)直接可视化乙醇诱导的 H3N2 病毒灭活。这一功能使 SAM 成为直接形态学评估消毒剂功效、补充感染性测定的宝贵工具。总之,SAM 为 H3N2 病毒的详细形态学研究和 抗病毒药物 药物评估提供了一种简单、快速、减少伪影的方法,为病毒学 EM 开辟了新的视角。

papers.title: 2010 and 2013 Incidence Peaks in Narcolepsy and Idiopathic Hypersomnia Linked to Type A H1N1 and Type B Victoria Influenza Strains.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Increased narcolepsy type‐1 (NT1) incidence rates were reported globally in 2010, linked to the H1N1 2009–2010 influenza pandemic and Pandemrix vaccination. A child‐specific NT1 peak was observed in Europe in 2013, further raising questions about the relationship between NT1 and influenza infections. This study analysed annual European incidence patterns of central disorders of hypersomnolence (CDH) in relation to influenza severity. All NT1 ( N = 981) and a combined group of narcolepsy type‐2 (NT2) and idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) ( N = 545) cases from eight European centers were studied from 1995 to 2019. Linear mixed models and Spearman correlations were applied to investigate the relationships between CDH incidence and the severity of preceding influenza seasons, including H1N1, H3N2, and for the Netherlands, influenza Type B Victoria and Yamagata. Peaks in NT1 incidence were present in 2010 and 2013, while a 2010 child‐specific peak was identified in NT2 and IH. Both groups showed a significantly positive correlation with H1N1 influenza severity and a negative correlation with H3N2. NT1 was also significantly associated with influenza Type B Victoria in the Netherlands, particularly in children. These findings suggest that, beyond H1N1, influenza Type B Victoria may be a novel trigger for NT1. Similar to NT1, the 2010 children peak in NT2 and IH may indicate possible immune‐related pathophysiologies linked to the 2009–2010 H1N1 pandemic. Further immunological studies are warranted to unravel the complexities of these relationships and their implications for CDH.

source_records.title: 2010 and 2013 Incidence Peaks in Narcolepsy and Idiopathic Hypersomnia Linked to Type A H1N1 and Type B Victoria Influenza Strains.
source_records.abstract: Increased narcolepsy type-1 (NT1) incidence rates were reported globally in 2010, linked to the H1N1 2009-2010 influenza pandemic and Pandemrix vaccination. A child-specific NT1 peak was observed in Europe in 2013, further raising questions about the relationship between NT1 and influenza infections. This study analysed annual European incidence patterns of central disorders of hypersomnolence (CDH) in relation to influenza severity. All NT1 (N = 981) and a combined group of narcolepsy type-2 (NT2) and idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) (N = 545) cases from eight European centers were studied from 1995 to 2019. Linear mixed models and Spearman correlations were applied to investigate the relationships between CDH incidence and the severity of preceding influenza seasons, including H1N1, H3N2, and for the Netherlands, influenza Type B Victoria and Yamagata. Peaks in NT1 incidence were present in 2010 and 2013, while a 2010 child-specific peak was identified in NT2 and IH. NT1 was also significantly associated with influenza Type B Victoria in the Netherlands, particularly in children. Similar to NT1, the 2010 children peak in NT2 and IH may indicate possible immune-related pathophysiologies linked to the 2009-2010 H1N1 pandemic. Further immunological studies are warranted to unravel the complexities of these relationships and their implications for CDH.

papers.title: Antiviral Treatment of Human Influenza A(H5N1) Infection: Treatment Timing, Clinical Outcomes, Virological Outcomes, and Antiviral Resistance: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Human influenza A(H5N1) infection remains a clinically important zoonotic disease, but evidence on antiviral effectiveness is limited by observational designs, heterogeneous treatment timing, and potentially overlapping patient populations. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data. Of 2,329 records identified, 22 publications were included. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Treatment within 2 days showed lower odds of death, although the overall estimate was not statistically significant (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–1.04). Among patients without respiratory failure at treatment initiation, earlier treatment was associated with lower mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.89). Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. Overall, oseltamivir, particularly when initiated early and before advanced respiratory failure, was associated with improved clinical outcomes, although causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.

papers.title: Genomic variability in the neuraminidase gene and antiviral susceptibility of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran (2023–2024)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The 2009 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pandemic caused substantial global morbidity and mortality. Mutations in the neuraminidase (NA) gene may influence viral evolution, immune evasion, and susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors, highlighting the importance of continuous molecular surveillance. Methods Between November 2023 and December 2024, 300 respiratory samples were collected from patients with acute respiratory infections in Shiraz, Iran, and screened for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 by real-time RT-PCR. Fourteen positive samples underwent full-length NA gene sequencing, amino acid substitution analysis, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking with oseltamivir and zanamivir. Phylogenetic comparison was performed using the historical pandemic reference strain A/California/07/2009 (NC_026434.1) to identify neuraminidase sequence divergence relative to the founding A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage. Results Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%). V241I and N369K are consistent with previously reported lineage-associated permissive substitutions in circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses, whereas N386K has been associated with alteration of an N-linked glycosylation site. Screening of the NA sequences for established WHO-recognized neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions identified no major known resistance markers, including H275Y and I223V. Molecular docking suggested preserved predicted binding of oseltamivir and zanamivir to neuraminidase. Conclusion Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz during 2023–2024 exhibited genetic variability in the neuraminidase gene while lacking established neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions. These findings provide sequence-based evidence consistent with the absence of established resistance markers among the analyzed isolates and emphasize the importance of continued molecular surveillance to monitor the emergence of clinically relevant NA mutations. Clinical Trial Registration Not applicable, as this study is observational and does not involve a clinical trial.

Mutations in the neuraminidase (NA) gene may influence viral evolution, immune evasion, and susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors, highlighting the importance of continuous molecular surveillance. Methods Between November 2023 and December 2024, 300 respiratory samples were collected from patients with acute respiratory infections in Shiraz, Iran, and screened for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 by real-time RT-PCR. Fourteen positive samples underwent full-length NA gene sequencing, amino acid substitution analysis, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking with oseltamivir and zanamivir. Phylogenetic comparison was performed using the historical pandemic reference strain A/California/07/2009 (NC_026434.1) to identify neuraminidase sequence divergence relative to the founding A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage. Results Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%). V241I and N369K are consistent with previously reported lineage-associated permissive substitutions in circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses, whereas N386K has been associated with alteration of an N-linked glycosylation site. Screening of the NA sequences for established WHO-recognized neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions identified no major known resistance markers, including H275Y and I223V. Molecular docking suggested preserved predicted binding of oseltamivir and zanamivir to neuraminidase. Conclusion Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz during 2023–2024 exhibited genetic variability in the neuraminidase gene while lacking established neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions. These findings provide sequence-based evidence consistent with the absence of established resistance markers among the analyzed isolates and emphasize the importance of continued molecular surveillance to monitor the emergence of clinically relevant NA mutations. Clinical Trial Registration Not applicable, as this study is observational and does not involve a clinical trial.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the genetic evolution of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses and their potential susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors, which is critical for monitoring antiviral resistance and informing public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and limited to 14 isolates, which may restrict generalizability. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on sequence analysis and molecular docking without clinical outcome data.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the genomic variability in the neuraminidase gene of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, during 2023–2024. A total of 300 respiratory samples were collected, and 14 were positive for the virus. The NA gene was sequenced, revealing 18 distinct amino acid substitutions. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K, which are associated with permissive mutations in circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. No major known resistance markers were identified, and molecular docking suggested preserved binding of oseltamivir and zanamivir. The study emphasizes the importance of molecular surveillance to monitor the emergence of clinically relevant NA mutations. However, the small sample size and observational design limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 2023 年至 2024 年期间从伊朗设拉子住院患者中分离出的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒神经氨酸酶基因的基因组变异,以评估对 抗病毒药物 易感性和病毒 进化 的潜在影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023年11月至2024年12月期间进行了一项横断面研究,收集了伊朗设拉子急性呼吸道感染患者的300份呼吸道样本,并分析了14份流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09阳性样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时 RT-PCR 对呼吸道样本进行流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 筛查。阳性样本进行全长NA基因测序、氨基酸取代分析、系统发育分析、结构建模以及与奥司他韦和扎那米韦的分子对接。
elements_zh.main_results: Sequence analysis identified 18 distinct amino acid substitutions in the NA gene among the 14 isolates. The most frequent substitutions were V241I and N369K (13/14, 92.9%), followed by N200S (4/14, 28.6%) and V394I (2/14, 14.3%).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,分析的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 分离株表现出 NA 基因的遗传变异性,但缺乏已确定的神经氨酸酶抑制剂耐药性相关取代,这凸显了对持续分子 监测 的需求。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒的 进化 基因及其对神经氨酸酶抑制剂的潜在敏感性的深入了解,这对于监测 抗病毒药物 耐药性和为公共卫生策略提供信息至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,仅限于 14 个分离株,这可能会限制普遍性。证据是中等的,因为它基于序列分析和分子对接,没有临床结果数据。

papers.title: The infectious unit of influenza A virus is a population of particles, not a single virion, as shown by absolute particle quantification
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) populations are characterized by a high prevalence of non-infectious virions, with particle-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratios typically ranging from 10 to 1,000. While "multiplicity reactivation" -the process by which incomplete viral genomes (IVGs) establish productive infection through co-infection- has long been hypothesized, its quantitative nature has remained elusive. In this study, we utilized a digital influenza assay to achieve absolute quantification of IAV particles, allowing us to define the particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) for precise evaluation. We combined this approach with a single-cell infection assay using microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to accurately assess infection outcomes across a wide range of pMOIs. Our analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) revealed a count-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratio of approximately 400, meaning only a tiny fraction of particles possesses infectivity. Remarkably, the infection rate in single-cell infection experiments followed a sigmoidal curve and reached saturation at a pMOI of only 5 to 10. This demonstrates that under high-pMOI conditions, productive infection is predominantly driven by genome complementation among incomplete particles rather than solely by fully infectious virions. On the other hand, mathematical model analysis based on these findings suggested that the functionality of each of the eight genomic segments within a virus particle follows a stochastic process, resulting in a probability distribution for the number of functional segments per particle. This mechanism proved exceptionally robust across multiple strains despite a 20-fold variation in CTPR values. Ultimately, these findings indicate that incomplete particles are not merely biological noise but active contributors to the infection process, significantly enhancing the infectivity and evolutionary flexibility of IAV. This study will provide a more refined understanding of influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments where multiple virus particles are present within a single respiratory droplet.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the infectious unit of influenza A virus by quantifying the ratio of particles to plaque-forming units (PFUs) and analyzing infection outcomes under varying particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) conditions. The researchers used a digital influenza assay and single-cell infection experiments with microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to assess the role of incomplete viral genomes in establishing productive infection. Their analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) strain revealed a PFU-to-particle ratio of approximately 400, with infection rates saturating at a pMOI of 5 to 10. These results suggest that genome complementation among incomplete particles, rather than fully infectious virions, drives productive infection under high-pMOI conditions. The findings have implications for understanding influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments with high viral particle concentrations. However, the study's reliance on a single strain may limit its generalizability, though the methodology is robust and the results are well-supported by the experimental design.

papers.abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 群体的特点是非感染性病毒体 患病率 较高,颗粒与噬菌斑形成单位 (PFU) 的比率通常为 10 至 1,000。虽然“多重再激活”——不完整病毒 基因组 (IVG) 通过共感染建立生产性感染的过程——长期以来一直被假设,但其定量性质仍然难以捉摸。在这项研究中,我们利用数字流感检测来实现 IAV 颗粒的绝对定量,从而使我们能够定义基于颗粒的感染复数 (pMOI) 进行精确评估。我们将这种方法与使用微区室容器和基于机器学习的自动细胞分类的单细胞感染测定相结合,以准确评估各种 pMOI 的感染结果。我们对 A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) 的分析显示,计数与噬菌斑形成单位 (PFU) 的比率约为 400,这意味着只有一小部分颗粒具有传染性。值得注意的是,单细胞感染实验中的感染率遵循 S 形曲线,并在 pMOI 仅 5 至 10 时达到饱和。这表明,在高 pMOI 条件下,生产性感染主要由不完整颗粒之间的 基因组 互补驱动,而不是仅由完全感染性病毒粒子驱动。另一方面,基于这些发现的数学模型分析表明,病毒颗粒内八个基因组片段中每一个的功能遵循随机过程,从而产生每个颗粒的功能片段数量的概率分布。尽管 CTPR 值存在 20 倍的变化,但该机制在多种菌株中被证明异常稳健。最终,这些发现表明,不完整颗粒不仅仅是生物噪音,而且是感染过程的积极贡献者,显着增强了 IAV 的感染性和进化灵活性。这项研究将为流感 传播 动态和风险评估提供更深入的了解,特别是在单个呼吸道飞沫中存在多个病毒颗粒的环境中。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,高 pMOI 条件下的生产性感染主要是由不完整颗粒之间的 基因组 互补驱动的,而不是完全感染性病毒粒子,这为了解不完整颗粒在流感 传播 中的作用提供了新的视角。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对流感 传播 动态和风险评估的更精细的了解,特别是在单个呼吸道飞沫中存在多个病毒颗粒的环境中。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于单一菌株,这可能会限制普遍性,但该方法是稳健的,并且结果得到了清晰而精确的实验设计的支持。

papers.title: Update to the CDC influenza A(H3) subtyping assay for improved detection of influenza A(H3N2) viruses, including subclade K viruses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza A(H3N2) viruses circulate globally and cause respiratory illness. The FDA-cleared CDC Human Influenza Virus Real-Time RT-PCR Influenza A (H3/H1pdm09) Subtyping assay is used to subtype seasonal influenza A viruses. However, emerging mutations in the H3 reverse primer region raised concerns about reduced assay sensitivity for contemporary circulating viruses. We updated the H3 assay by redesigning the reverse primer to target a more conserved region of the hemagglutinin gene, and incorporating minor adjustments into the forward primer and probe. Analytical sensitivity, inclusivity, and exclusivity evaluations were performed using cultured influenza viruses, synthetic RNA, and panels of non-influenza respiratory pathogens. Clinical performance was evaluated using seasonal A(H3N2) residual respiratory specimens. The updated assay (H3_v2) demonstrated analytical sensitivity comparable to or improved over the initial H3 assay, with a limit of detection of approximately 10 1.7 –10 2.1 EID 50 /mL and five copies of RNA per reaction. Improved performance was observed for viruses containing A21G with T23G, T23C, or T23A double mismatches in the reverse primer, with a measurable Ct value shift between the initial H3 and H3_v2 assay. The assay showed 100% agreement with expected results in 139 clinical specimens, and no cross-reactivity with other influenza subtypes or other respiratory pathogens. These findings indicate the updated H3_v2 assay improves sensitivity for contemporary and emerging seasonal A(H3N2) viruses while maintaining high specificity. This update ensures continued reliable detection of seasonal A(H3N2), including genetically drifted A(H3N2) viruses, such as the recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and supports global influenza surveillance and diagnostic preparedness. IMPORTANCE Accurate detection and subtyping of influenza A(H3N2) viruses are essential for clinical diagnostics, outbreak response, and global influenza surveillance. The emergence and fixation of mutations leading to primer mismatches in the FDA-cleared CDC A(H3) real-time RT-PCR assay raised concerns about reduced sensitivity for contemporary circulating A(H3N2) viruses. To address this, we redesigned the reverse primer and optimized additional assay components to improve detection of currently circulating seasonal A(H3N2) viruses. The updated H3_v2 assay restores and enhances sensitivity, including for viruses harboring key reverse primer mismatches, while maintaining high specificity and complete agreement with clinical specimens. This update ensures reliable detection of seasonal influenza A(H3N2) and A(H3N2) variant viruses, including recently emerged A(H3N2) subclade K viruses, and strengthens diagnostic preparedness and surveillance capacity nationally and internationally.

papers.title: Development of lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines against swine influenza
papers.abstract: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) cause highly contagious respiratory disease in pigs and pose zoonotic risk due to bidirectional transmission between humans and swine. Managing IAV-S, particularly the H1 subtype, in pigs is vital both to prevent interspecies transmission and to protect the swine industry. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated mRNA vaccines encoding specific viral antigens offer a rapid, adaptable platform well-suited for targeting rapidly evolving influenza strains. Hemagglutinin (HA), the viral protein that initiates infection, is a critical target for vaccination due to its central role in influenza infection and its antigenic diversity. This study aimed to design and generate three mRNA-LNP vaccine candidates encoding distinct HA antigens: a Taiwan porcine H1, a swine-to-human H1, and a consensus H1. We then evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-reactive potential of these candidates in a mouse model. In vivo evaluation demonstrated that the swine-to-human H1 vaccine candidate induced the broadest humoral IgG response across all three HA antigens, whereas the Taiwan porcine H1 candidate elicited the narrowest cross-reactive immunity. Serum derived from mice-immunized with all three candidate vaccines neutralized the Taiwan porcine H1N2 virus to varying degrees. However, neither intramuscular nor intranasal administration induced mucosal immunity. These results suggest while the swine-to-human HA construct shows strong potential for providing broad systemic immunity, the consensus HA construct requires further optimization. An effective swine influenza vaccine strategy may require a combined intramuscular and intranasal approach to ensure comprehensive systemic and mucosal immunity, including the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.

Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.

papers.title_zh: 抗猪流感脂质纳米颗粒mRNA 疫苗的开发
papers.source_body_en: Swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) cause highly contagious respiratory disease in pigs and pose zoonotic risk due to bidirectional transmission between humans and swine. Managing IAV-S, particularly the H1 subtype, in pigs is vital both to prevent interspecies transmission and to protect the swine industry. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated mRNA vaccines encoding specific viral antigens offer a rapid, adaptable platform well-suited for targeting rapidly evolving influenza strains. Hemagglutinin (HA), the viral protein that initiates infection, is a critical target for vaccination due to its central role in influenza infection and its antigenic diversity. This study aimed to design and generate three mRNA-LNP vaccine candidates encoding distinct HA antigens: a Taiwan porcine H1, a swine-to-human H1, and a consensus H1. We then evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-reactive potential of these candidates in a mouse model. In vivo evaluation demonstrated that the swine-to-human H1 vaccine candidate induced the broadest humoral IgG response across all three HA antigens, whereas the Taiwan porcine H1 candidate elicited the narrowest cross-reactive immunity. Serum derived from mice-immunized with all three candidate vaccines neutralized the Taiwan porcine H1N2 virus to varying degrees. However, neither intramuscular nor intranasal administration induced mucosal immunity. These results suggest while the swine-to-human HA construct shows strong potential for providing broad systemic immunity, the consensus HA construct requires further optimization. An effective swine influenza vaccine strategy may require a combined intramuscular and intranasal approach to ensure comprehensive systemic and mucosal immunity, including the induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Further analysis of the cross-protection and cellular immunity elicited by these candidates is necessary.
papers.abstract_zh: 甲型猪流感病毒 (IAV-S) 可引起猪的高度传染性呼吸道疾病,并由于人与猪之间的双向 传播 造成人畜共患风险。管理猪的 IAV-S,特别是 H1 亚型,对于预防跨种 传播 和保护养猪业至关重要。脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 封装的 mRNA 疫苗 编码特定病毒抗原,提供了一个快速、适应性强的平台,非常适合针对快速进化的流感病毒株。血凝素 (HA) 是一种启动感染的病毒蛋白,由于其在流感感染中的核心作用及其抗原多样性,是 疫苗接种 的关键靶点。本研究旨在设计和生成三种编码不同 HA 抗原的 mRNA-LNP 疫苗 候选药物:台湾猪 H1、猪转人 H1 和共有 H1。然后我们在小鼠模型中评估了这些候选物的免疫原性和交叉反应潜力。体内评估表明,猪对人 H1 疫苗 候选药物在所有三种 HA 抗原上诱导了最广泛的体液 IgG 反应,而台湾猪 H1 候选药物则引发了最窄的交叉反应免疫。用所有三种候选 疫苗 免疫的小鼠的血清在不同程度上中和了台湾猪 H1N2 病毒。然而,肌内或鼻内给药均未诱导粘膜免疫。这些结果表明,虽然猪到人的 HA 构建体显示出提供广泛的系统免疫的强大潜力,但共有的 HA 构建体需要进一步优化。有效的猪流感 疫苗 策略可能需要结合肌内和鼻内方法,以确保全面的全身和粘膜免疫,包括诱导广泛中和抗体。有必要对这些候选物引起的交叉保护和细胞免疫进行进一步分析。

papers.title: Computationally designed multisubtype epigraph vaccine confers broad-spectrum protection against H1 and H3 swine influenza A viruses
papers.abstract: H1 and H3 subtype swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) threaten global agricultural economies and pose zoonotic risks, yet conventional vaccines provide limited protection against their vast antigenic diversity. Here, we developed a multisubtype vaccine utilizing adenoviral vectors expressing computationally designed H1 and H3 epigraph hemagglutinin (HA) immunogens. In mice, this All-in-One formulation elicited balanced humoral and cellular immunity and demonstrated neutralizing breadth against diverse IAV-S isolates compared to a commercially available vaccine. The multisubtype delivery system elicited concurrent immunity and protection against both H1 and H3 subtypes. The All-in-One vaccine conferred protection against heterologous H1 and H3 challenges and did not exacerbate clinical morbidity characteristic of mismatched vaccination. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of computationally optimized and multiplexed vaccines providing broad-spectrum protection against evolving influenza viruses without compromising safety.

papers.title_zh: 计算设计的多亚型铭文 疫苗 具有针对 H1 和 H3 猪甲型流感病毒的广谱保护
papers.source_body_en: H1 and H3 subtype swine influenza A viruses (IAV-S) threaten global agricultural economies and pose zoonotic risks, yet conventional vaccines provide limited protection against their vast antigenic diversity. Here, we developed a multisubtype vaccine utilizing adenoviral vectors expressing computationally designed H1 and H3 epigraph hemagglutinin (HA) immunogens. In mice, this All-in-One formulation elicited balanced humoral and cellular immunity and demonstrated neutralizing breadth against diverse IAV-S isolates compared to a commercially available vaccine. The multisubtype delivery system elicited concurrent immunity and protection against both H1 and H3 subtypes. The All-in-One vaccine conferred protection against heterologous H1 and H3 challenges and did not exacerbate clinical morbidity characteristic of mismatched vaccination. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of computationally optimized and multiplexed vaccines providing broad-spectrum protection against evolving influenza viruses without compromising safety.

Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Cross-Protection against Influenza A(H5) Clade 2.3.4.4b Viruses after A(H1N1)pdm09 Infection Suggested citation for this article Abstract We challenged ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess cross-protection. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. Influenza A(H5) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have spread widely among wild birds and poultry and caused infections in mammals, including humans, raising public health concerns (1). A case of human infection with H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was reported in Washington, USA during 2025; the patient subsequently died, representing the second fatal A(H5) case in the United States (1,2). A(H1) and A(H5) hemagglutinins (HAs) belong to influenza A virus phylogenetic group 1. Most antibodies targeting the HA stalk, a conserved, membrane-proximal region of HA, are cross-reactive with HAs within the same phylogenetic group (3). Studies have demonstrated that previous influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection can provide some protection against H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses (4,5). The emergence of H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus raises questions about whether previous A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity confers similar protection against A(H5) viruses bearing antigenically distinct neuraminidases (NAs). We used a preimmune ferret model to compare cross-protection conferred by previous A(H1N1)pdm09 infection against A(H5) viruses with homologous or heterologous NA subtypes. We conducted all experiments with H5N5 and H5N1 viruses in a Biosafety Level 3 enhanced facility with approval from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. We intranasally inoculated 12 ferrets serologically naive to seasonal influenza viruses with 103 PFUs of A(H1N1)pdm09 A/Nebraska/14/2019 virus. We confirmed seroconversion 3 months postinfection by using a hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay, which detects antibodies that inhibit HA-mediated hemagglutination, with a geometric mean titer of 320 (95% CI 245.3–417.3) (Appendix Figure, panel A). Using previously described multiplex binding assays (6), we detected high levels of antibodies binding to the head of A(H1N1)pdm09, but not HA head or ectodomain from H5N1 or H5N5 viruses, and antibodies binding to N1 NAs from A(H1N1)pdm09 and H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not N5 NA from H5N5 virus. In addition, we detected antibodies binding to the group 1 HA stalk derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 virus (Appendix Figure, panels B, C). We then intranasally challenged those animals, referred to as preimmune ferrets, with 104 PFU of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b A/Washington/239/2024 or H5N5 A/Washington/2148/2025 virus (6 ferrets per virus), alongside naive control groups without previous influenza immunity. We euthanized 3 ferrets per group on day 4 postinfection to assess viral dissemination; we monitored the remaining animals for clinical signs, weight loss, viral shedding in nasal washes, and virus presence in throat and rectal swabs. Severe disease, characterized by lethargy, fever, and substantial weight loss (maximum 13.8% in H5N1 virus inoculated ferrets and 18.4% in H5N5 virus inoculated ferrets), developed in naive ferrets inoculated with H5N1 or H5N5 viruses. We euthanized all animals on postinfection days 5–6 for H5N1 virus–inoculated ferrets and days 6–10 for H5N5 virus–inoculated ferrets after they reached predefined humane endpoints, consistent with previous reports (7,8). In contrast, preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N1 virus exhibited minimal disease, a mean maximum weight loss of 2.4%, and 100% survival (Figure 1, panels A–C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N5 also showed reduced disease severity (mean maximum weight loss 7.6%); however, 1 animal reached a humane endpoint on day 7 postinfection (Figure 1, panels B, C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with either H5N1 or H5N5 virus shed similar levels of virus in nasal wash samples during days 1–4 postinfection (range of mean peak titers 103.8–105.2 PFU/mL) as naive controls but exhibited reduced titers in throat swab samples on day 4 for H5N5 virus and days 2 and 3 for H5N1 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Viral clearance from nasal washes occurred 2–4 days earlier in preimmune ferrets. We detected H5N1 virus less frequently in rectal swab samples from preimmune animals than from naive controls, whereas we did not observe that reduction for ferrets infected with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus preimmunity did not substantially reduce viral titers in the upper respiratory tract (nasal turbinates) or soft palate after H5N1 or H5N5 virus challenge (Figure 2, panels C, D). However, A(H1N1)pdm09 preimmunity largely prevented viral dissemination to the lower respiratory tract (trachea and lungs) and extrapulmonary tissues for both viruses, with only sporadic low-level viral detection. However, intestinal viral titers were comparable between preimmune and naive ferrets challenged with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels C, D). Detection of group 1 HA stalk antibodies after A(H1N1)pdm09 infection (Appendix Figure), together with previous evidence of HA stalk-mediated cross-protection against disease caused by the influenza A viruses within the same phylogenetic group (3,9), suggests that cross-reactive HA stalk antibodies might contribute to protection against A(H5) viruses. In addition, N1 cross-reactivity might further enhance protection against H5N1 virus. Consistent with our findings, limited N5 cross-reactivity has been reported in humans despite detectable N1 responses (10). Further studies using H5-specific HA stalk antigens and functional assays are needed to determine the contribution of cross-reactive antibodies and cellular immunity to protection against zoonotic influenza A viruses. Our findings showed that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 viral infection conferred partial cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 viruses in ferrets, reducing disease severity, lethality, and viral dissemination. Dr. Sun is a microbiologist in the Influenza Division, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, Georgia, USA. Her research primarily focuses on using the ferret model to understand influenza virus pathogenicity and transmissibility. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. Influenza A(H5) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have spread widely among wild birds and poultry and caused infections in mammals, including humans, raising public health concerns (1). A case of human infection with H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was reported in Washington, USA during 2025; the patient subsequently died, representing the second fatal A(H5) case in the United States (1,2). A(H1) and A(H5) hemagglutinins (HAs) belong to influenza A virus phylogenetic group 1. Most antibodies targeting the HA stalk, a conserved, membrane-proximal region of HA, are cross-reactive with HAs within the same phylogenetic group (3). Studies have demonstrated that previous influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection can provide some protection against H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses (4,5). The emergence of H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus raises questions about whether previous A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity confers similar protection against A(H5) viruses bearing antigenically distinct neuraminidases (NAs). We used a preimmune ferret model to compare cross-protection conferred by previous A(H1N1)pdm09 infection against A(H5) viruses with homologous or heterologous NA subtypes. We conducted all experiments with H5N5 and H5N1 viruses in a Biosafety Level 3 enhanced facility with approval from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. We intranasally inoculated 12 ferrets serologically naive to seasonal influenza viruses with 103 PFUs of A(H1N1)pdm09 A/Nebraska/14/2019 virus. We confirmed seroconversion 3 months postinfection by using a hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay, which detects antibodies that inhibit HA-mediated hemagglutination, with a geometric mean titer of 320 (95% CI 245.3–417.3) (Appendix Figure, panel A). Using previously described multiplex binding assays (6), we detected high levels of antibodies binding to the head of A(H1N1)pdm09, but not HA head or ectodomain from H5N1 or H5N5 viruses, and antibodies binding to N1 NAs from A(H1N1)pdm09 and H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not N5 NA from H5N5 virus. In addition, we detected antibodies binding to the group 1 HA stalk derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 virus (Appendix Figure, panels B, C). We then intranasally challenged those animals, referred to as preimmune ferrets, with 104 PFU of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b A/Washington/239/2024 or H5N5 A/Washington/2148/2025 virus (6 ferrets per virus), alongside naive control groups without previous influenza immunity. We euthanized 3 ferrets per group on day 4 postinfection to assess viral dissemination; we monitored the remaining animals for clinical signs, weight loss, viral shedding in nasal washes, and virus presence in throat and rectal swabs. Severe disease, characterized by lethargy, fever, and substantial weight loss (maximum 13.8% in H5N1 virus inoculated ferrets and 18.4% in H5N5 virus inoculated ferrets), developed in naive ferrets inoculated with H5N1 or H5N5 viruses. We euthanized all animals on postinfection days 5–6 for H5N1 virus–inoculated ferrets and days 6–10 for H5N5 virus–inoculated ferrets after they reached predefined humane endpoints, consistent with previous reports (7,8). In contrast, preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N1 virus exhibited minimal disease, a mean maximum weight loss of 2.4%, and 100% survival (Figure 1, panels A–C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N5 also showed reduced disease severity (mean maximum weight loss 7.6%); however, 1 animal reached a humane endpoint on day 7 postinfection (Figure 1, panels B, C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with either H5N1 or H5N5 virus shed similar levels of virus in nasal wash samples during days 1–4 postinfection (range of mean peak titers 103.8–105.2 PFU/mL) as naive controls but exhibited reduced titers in throat swab samples on day 4 for H5N5 virus and days 2 and 3 for H5N1 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Viral clearance from nasal washes occurred 2–4 days earlier in preimmune ferrets. We detected H5N1 virus less frequently in rectal swab samples from preimmune animals than from naive controls, whereas we did not observe that reduction for ferrets infected with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus preimmunity did not substantially reduce viral titers in the upper respiratory tract (nasal turbinates) or soft palate after H5N1 or H5N5 virus challenge (Figure 2, panels C, D). However, A(H1N1)pdm09 preimmunity largely prevented viral dissemination to the lower respiratory tract (trachea and lungs) and extrapulmonary tissues for both viruses, with only sporadic low-level viral detection. However, intestinal viral titers were comparable between preimmune and naive ferrets challenged with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels C, D). Detection of group 1 HA stalk antibodies after A(H1N1)pdm09 infection (Appendix Figure), together with previous evidence of HA stalk-mediated cross-protection against disease caused by the influenza A viruses within the same phylogenetic group (3,9), suggests that cross-reactive HA stalk antibodies might contribute to protection against A(H5) viruses. In addition, N1 cross-reactivity might further enhance protection against H5N1 virus. Consistent with our findings, limited N5 cross-reactivity has been reported in humans despite detectable N1 responses (10). Further studies using H5-specific HA stalk antigens and functional assays are needed to determine the contribution of cross-reactive antibodies and cellular immunity to protection against zoonotic influenza A viruses. Our findings showed that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 viral infection conferred partial cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 viruses in ferrets, reducing disease severity, lethality, and viral dissemination. Her research primarily focuses on using the ferret model to understand influenza virus pathogenicity and transmissibility. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether prior infection with A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. Ferrets infected with A(H1N1)pdm09 were challenged with H5N1 and H5N5 viruses, and results showed partial protection against both, with slightly less protection against H5N5. The findings suggest that HA stalk antibodies may mediate cross-protection, which has implications for understanding immune responses to emerging H5 viruses. The study's use of a controlled ferret model provides strong evidence, though limitations include the absence of human data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估先前感染 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒是否可以提供针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒的交叉保护,这些病毒由于在鸟类和哺乳动物中传播而引起了公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了免疫前雪貂模型,其中 12 只雪貂在血清学上对 季节性流感 病毒不敏感,并用 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒对它们进行攻击。每组三只雪貂在感染后第 4 天被安乐死,以评估病毒传播情况。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员用 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 病毒感染雪貂,并使用血凝抑制 (HAI) 测定证实了血清转化。然后,他们用 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒攻击这些未免疫的雪貂,并监测临床症状、体重减轻和病毒脱落。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,先前的 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 免疫可对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供部分保护,但对 H5N5 病毒的保护略有减弱,这可能是由于缺乏交叉反应性 N5 神经氨酸酶抗体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 感染的免疫力可能对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒提供一些交叉保护,突出了 HA 茎抗体在这种交叉反应中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解针对新出现的 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒的交叉保护具有重要意义,这可以为 监测 和 疫苗 的开发策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于雪貂模型,并未考虑人类 免疫应答,但由于受控的实验设计和明确的结果,证据是强有力的。

analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,先前的 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 免疫可对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供部分保护,但对 H5N5 病毒的保护略有减弱,这可能是由于缺乏交叉反应性 N5 神经氨酸酶抗体。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 感染的免疫力可能对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒提供一些交叉保护,突出了 HA 茎抗体在这种交叉反应中的潜在作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解针对新出现的 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒的交叉保护具有重要意义,这可以为 监测 和 疫苗 的开发策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于雪貂模型,并未考虑人类 免疫应答,但由于受控的实验设计和明确的结果,证据是强有力的。

NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Monday, November 16, 2026 South Korea APQA Issues HPAI Alert #19,418 While H5N1 remains the primary global HPAI threat, since 2022 we've watched a divergent subtype - H5N5 - establish itself and persist in high latitude regions of the Northern Hemisphere, and last year we followed the first incursion of an H5N9 subtype into South Korea (see South Korea: H5N9 Rising). South Korea's MAFRA reported 62 outbreaks in poultry over the 2025-2026 avian flu season, and of those, 57 were H5N1 while only 5 (8%) were H5N9. Nine days ago, in South Korea: MAFRA Reports 2 Outbreaks of HPAI H5N9 in Poultry & Ducks, we looked at early season reports indicating 2 of the first 3 poultry outbreaks this fall were H5N9. Since then 3 more poultry farm outbreaks have been reported (Ganghwa, Jincheon, Paju ), which MAFRA has described as a `mix' of H5N9 and H5N1. Yesterday, MAFRA reported a non-farm `ornamental bird' operation was positive for HPAI H5, with NA typing pending. Today, local media is reporting it to be H5N9, but again, I haven't found official confirmation. This year South Korean avian flu reports (which are already hampered by machine translation) seem less detailed. Below, you'll find their Risk Alert lists 6 poultry outbreaks, and 10 wild bird detections, but doesn't provide a breakdown by subtype. It would appear that somewhere between 3 and 5 of the first 7 outbreaks in South Korea this fall are due to H5N9. Even assuming the lowest number, that would represent a significant shift from the 8% reported last year. First the AQPA statement, after which I'll have a bit more. Animal Quarantine Agency Issues Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI) Risk Alert Department in charge Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency Author Lee Hyun-jik 82 2026-11-14 The Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency ( Acting Director Jeong Seung-gyo , hereinafter the Agency ) issued a “ Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI ) Risk Advisory ” on November 13 as the risk of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI ) outbreaks in domestic poultry farms increased , and simultaneously disseminated the quarantine measures to poultry farms , livestock facilities , and vehicle drivers nationwide through text messages , notifications , etc. Measures to raise awareness among livestock stakeholders and strengthen disease control measures in accordance with the Avian Influenza Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) when warning signs, such as the detection of multiple AI antigens in wild birds, occur. Since highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) antigens were detected in wild bird droppings collected at Suncheon Bay in Gwangju, Jeollanam-do (October 12 ), a total of 10 cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) have been detected to date. In poultry farms as well, following the outbreak at a laying hen farm in Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi-do (November 3), a total of 6 cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) have occurred at a broiler duck farm in Jangheung, Gwangju, Jeollanam-do (November 5 ) , a laying hen farm in Yeoju , Gyeonggi -do (November 6 ), a laying hen farm in Ganghwa, Incheon (November 11), a breeding duck farm in Jincheon, Chungcheongbuk-do (November 12), and a quail farm in Paju, Gyeonggi-do ( November 12 ) . In particular , during this winter season, two serotypes, H5N1 and H5N9 , have been identified and are occurring frequently in a short period , making thorough disease control management necessary . * ( Wild Birds ) 10 cases ( Suncheon Suncheon Bay 1, Gimpo Lower Han River 2, Yongin Cheongmicheon 1, Hongcheon Yangdeokwoncheon 2, Jeonnam Gwangju Gwangsan-gu Hwangnyonggang 1, Yeoju Namhangang 1, Nonsan Yeonsancheon 1, Jeongeup Dongjingang 1) * ( Poultry Farms ) 6 cases ( Yeoncheon Laying Hen 1, Jangheung Broiler Duck 1, Yeoju Laying Hen 1, Ganghwa Laying Hen 1, Jincheon Breeding Duck 1, Paju Quail 1) In addition , monitoring of the movement of migratory birds equipped with GPS trackers revealed that the southward migration of birds appears to be in full swing, as evidenced by the confirmation that mallards residing in Baiqing, Jilin Province, China, migrated south to Korea on November 6 and were inhabiting Uljin, North Gyeongsang Province , on November 7. In particular , the risk is increasing, as highly pathogenic AI was detected in Mandarin ducks captured in the Hwangryong River in Gwangju , South Jeolla Province, and Eurasian wigeon captured in Yeonsan Stream in Nonsan, South Chungcheong Province . Meanwhile , in Japan , after highly pathogenic AI antigens were detected in wild birds and the environment ( water ) in Akita, Hokkaido , and Kagoshima prefectures on November 2 , suspected cases of highly pathogenic AI were reported at a laying hen farm in Kyoto Prefecture (200,000 birds ) and laying hens in Chiba Prefecture (40,000 birds ) . * Japan Outbreak Status : 3 cases of wild birds ( including environment ) ( 2 H5N1 , 1 H5 ) , 2 cases reported from poultry farms Given the current status of wild bird arrivals in Korea, antigen detection, and outbreaks in neighboring countries , there is a very high risk of transmission of highly pathogenic avian influenza (AI) virus from wild birds to poultry farms this winter . Accordingly , the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency has issued a “ Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (AI) Risk Advisory ” to raise awareness among livestock industry stakeholders and strengthen disease control measures . It has urged poultry farms to comply with disease control rules , including: △ two- stage disinfection of vehicles entering the farm ; △ wearing protective clothing and dedicated shoes and thorough personal disinfection for those entering the farm ; △ closing secondary entrances and back doors of barns without anterooms ; and △ changing into dedicated boots and disinfecting hands in the anteroom when entering the barn. At the same time , the agency plans to further strengthen inspections through the central inspection team of the Animal Disease Control Center regarding whether livestock vehicles are entering farms and whether disinfection is being carried out at designated disinfection facilities . Jeong Seung-kyo, Acting Head of the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency, stated , “ With the recent increase in farm outbreaks and the expected arrival of migratory birds starting in November , we are in a grave situation where outbreaks could occur anywhere in the country, ” and urged poultry farmers to “ thoroughly implement farm-level quarantine measures, taking into account that virus contamination levels around farms and outside livestock barns are also rising significantly . ” In early 2014, an upstart H5N8 subtype abruptly appeared in South Korea, rapidly decimated their poultry industry, and then spread globally via migratory birds. Over the next 6 years it became the dominant global HPAI subtype, and sparked massive epizootics in Europe, the United States, and the Middle East. Its saving grace was that - unlike older H5N1 strains - it appeared less likely to infect humans. It wasn't until 2021 that the first human infections were reported (see Russian Media Reports 7 Human Infections With Avian H5N8), and by then H5N1 was on the upswing. While the significance or ultimate impact of this apparent rise in H5N9 is far from clear, it does remind us that HPAI is constantly changing. And that what first appears in South Korea, doesn't always stay in South Korea. Sunday, November 15, 2026 Canada: CFIA Statement on H5N1 Outbreak At Saskatchewan Poultry Show Posted on Saskatchewan Poultry Association Group Facebook page #19,417 Yesterday, CBC News reported Avian flu outbreak at national poultry show spreads to other provinces: CFIA, citing receipt of a CFIA statement. I was unable to find it on the CFIA website, but did locate a copy on the Saskatchewan Poultry Association Group Facebook page (above). The text reads: Canadian Food Inspection Agency November 13, 2026 Important Notice: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) Exposure In Canada, Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) is a federally reportable disease under the Health of Animals Act for all animals, meaning any suspected or confirmed case must be reported immediately to the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). The CFIA has detected a case of highly pathogenic avian influenza associated with a poultry show held on November 07, 2026 by the American Poultry Association for District 11 in Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan. If you showed birds at the event, or purchased or sold birds at the event, please immediately contact the CFIA's sick bird call line at 1-403-338-5225 if the CFIA has not already contacted you. If you attended the event without showing, purchasing, or selling birds, but you have birds of your own at home, please monitor them for any signs of illness. The incubation period of HPAL ranges from 2 to 14 days and it can be transmitted to other birds in multiple ways, such as birds having direct or indirect contact with infected birds, or through the movement of contaminated clothing/footwear to other groups of birds. If your own birds display any clinical signs which could be associated with highly pathogenic avian influenza (ex. lethargic, not eating, swollen cyes/wattles/combs, respiratory signs, unexpected decrease in egg production, or deaths), immediately contact the CFIA's sick bird call line at 1-403-338-5225 to report this suspicion of Thank you for your cooperation in helping to control this outbreak. For more information regarding highly pathogenic avian influenza, visit: https://inspection.canada.ca/en/animal-health/terrestrial-animals/diseases/reportable/avian-influenza CFIA reported their first outbreak in poultry of the fall on September 10th, followed by a slow ramping up of cases through the rest of September (n=8) and October (n=13). Over the past 5 days, however, the number of outbreaks has risen sharply (n=11). Poultry exhibitions tend to be held in the fall, since adult birds molt in the summer and typically regain peak appearance in October and November, chicks hatched in the spring reach full adult size by autumn, and transport of birds is easier during cooler weather (less heat stress). Unfortunately, this also corresponds with the fall bird migration and increased risk of HPAI. While this Saskatchewan event appears to be one of the last big events this year in Canada, the American Poultry Association still lists a number of large events scheduled over the next two months. HPAI outbreaks traced to poultry exhibitions in North America have been rare thus far due to biosecurity measures in place and a willingness to cancel events, but we have seen numerous outbreaks linked to live bird markets (see USDA Reports Another H5N1 Outbreak at a Live Bird Market (Pennsylvania)). Each year it seems to get a little bit harder to prevent and/or contain HPAI. While fortuitous evolution might someday attenuate those risks, so far, we've seen little sign of that happening. Saturday, November 14, 2026 For When The Bough Breaks CDC Infographic #19,416 Over the past 20 years the secondary focus of this blog has been on personal preparedness, and the growing fragility our our increasingly high-tech dependent infrastructure. Much of this comes from my 15 years of living aboard boats, and constantly thinking about what could fail (usually at the worst possible moment), and how to limit its impact. The events of the past few days (Microsoft outage, FAA 4-hour emergency groundstop, and several very large cyber-heists) remind us how fragile or vulnerable our systems are. Last January, in NERC: Long-Term Reliability Assessment (Jan 2026), we looked (again) at growing concerns over the stability of the nation's electrical grid, followed last May by NERC Issues Level 3 Alert As Grid Faces `Unprecedented Challenges' Due to Surge In Large Power Consumers. Every four years the ASCE (American Society of Civil Engineers) releases a report card on America’s infrastructure, and their most recent report (2025) warns that our cumulative GPA for infrastructure sits at only a C, and one of our most vulnerable infrastructures is the electrical grid (D+). This D+ rating is shared by Aviation, Dams, Roads, Levees, Wastewater, and Schools, while Stormwater and Transit are rated even lower. And every day that passes without addressing these problems only increases the risks. Regardless of what conspires to bring these systems down (age, neglect, deliberate sabotage, etc.), the impact will often first fall upon the American public. I was in New Orleans 5 weeks after Hurricane Katrina in 2005, and there was still no electricity, or running water, across most of the city. The streets were lined with debris and dead refrigerators filled with rotting food, pharmacies were still boarded up, and any semblance of normalcy was still months away. In 2014's Water, Water, Everywhere But Not A Drop To Drink we saw hundreds of thousands of Ohio residents without potable water for days due to harmful toxins produced by a microcystis algae bloom. This was neither the first or last such event. A similar emergency was declared in Oregon in 2018 (see Tapping Into Your Preps). (2018 advisory) Eight years ago, in NIAC: Surviving A Catastrophic Power Outage, we looked at a presidential commission's report on the risks of a major, prolonged, grid collapse. https://www.hsdl.org/?view&did=819354 This 92-page report was released a little more than a year after hurricane ravaged Puerto Rico suffered the longest (11-month) grid failure in American History and a year following another report - DHS: NIAC Cyber Threat Report - August 2017 - that warned of growing cyber threats to our critical infrastructure and called for `bold, decisive actions'. Over the past 10 years I've gone through 2 hurricane-induced extended (4-7 day) power outages, and one prolonged community well failure, that had me relying on my personal preps for food, water, and power for days. Yet I've been lucky. Many others have had to deal with far worse. In recent months we've seen increased calls by governments around the world for increased personal preparedness (see UK National Risk Register 2026 - Urges Citizen Preparedness). While the reasons given are often vague, concerns over natural or man-made disasters appear to be rising. California and the Pacific Northwest are bracing for what could be an unprecedented winter El Nino (see California Declares State of Emergency to Bolster Statewide El Niño Preparedness), while Florida has just completed its first El Nino Awareness week. This year, I've beefed up my solar preps, adding a second solar panel, and additional battery capacity (see #NPM26: It's a 12 Volt Life). I've added a battery operated camp shower, a better shortwave radio, and have recently gone through and thrown out long out-of-date canned food from my pantry. None of which guarantees I'll come away unscathed from an emergency, but I firmly believe it greatly increases my chances. While I'm far from a luddite (I love my gadgets), I know that things break. And as a (former) computer programer I know the more complicated a system becomes, the more likely it is to fail and the harder it will be to fix. Given the complexities of our aging infrastructure, it follows that more failures can be expected. Whether due to natural disasters, failed upgrades, `bad actors', or simply bad luck . . . the odds increase a little each day that you will be adversely affected. The question isn't whether another emergency will arise, it is whether you and your family will be ready to deal with it. How you should prepare will depend upon where you live, the likely threats you will face, and logistical, physical, or financial limitations. I'm unlikely to freeze to death here in Florida, but heat-related deaths are relatively common. And while Southern California doesn't worry about hurricanes, they do have a significant seismic threat. How you go about preparing may be different, but your goals are pretty similar. So if the power goes out today - and stays out for a week - do you have? A battery operated NWS Emergency Radio to find out what was going on, and to get vital instructions from emergency officials A decent first-aid kit, so that you can treat injuries Enough non-perishable food and water on hand to feed and hydrate your family (including pets) for the duration A way to provide light when the grid is down. A way to cook safely without electricity A way to purify or filter water A way to handle basic sanitation and waste disposal. A way to stay cool (fans) or warm when the power is out. A small supply of cash to use in case credit/debit machines are not working An emergency plan, including meeting places, emergency out-of-state contact numbers, a disaster buddy, and in case you must evacuate, a bug-out bag Spare supply of essential prescription medicines that you or your family may need A way to entertain yourself, or your kids, during a prolonged blackout A good place to get started is by visiting Ready.gov, or by hitting this link which will serve up a series of my preparedness blogs. While you may go years without needing it, with emergency preparedness it is better to be ready 5 years too soon than 5 minutes too late. papers.title: Oxidized Cellulose Nanofiber Hydrogels for 3D Airway Spheroids and Influenza Infection Modeling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Micro‐physiological systems (MPS) that recapitulate tissue architecture and immune competence are urgently needed to model respiratory viral infections and accelerate antiviral discovery. Here, we create an airway spheroid‐based MPS supported by an oxidized cellulose nanofiber (OCNF) hydrogel, which provides a hydrated, extracellular matrix (ECM) mimetic nanofibrillar microenvironment and supports stable long‐term 3D culture. Airway epithelial‐like spheroids are generated either from Calu‐3 cells alone or as immunocompetent co‐culture spheroids incorporating polarized THP‐1 macrophage‐like cells to capture epithelial‐immune crosstalk. The OCNF platform promotes rapid spheroid self‐assembly within 6 days and preserves structural integrity for ≥ 20 days, allowing longitudinal interrogation of influenza A virus replication and host innate immune responses. Notably, the model reveals that human bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exert potent antiviral activity, significantly reducing influenza infection through activation of interferon (IFN)‐associated pathways, including MX1, OAS1, and STAT1. Together, this OCNF hydrogel‐enabled airway spheroid MPS provides a scalable and reproducible test‐bed for mechanistic studies and preclinical evaluation of antiviral interventions and establishes an in vitro platform toward personalized patient‐relevant respiratory infection models.
