analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨Clostridium sporogenes(一种人类厌氧共生菌,能够产生吲哚-3-丙酸(IPA))在流感A病毒(IAV)感染中的潜在保护作用,鉴于肠道微生物群及其代谢产物在呼吸道感染期间对肺部保护的作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及感染流感A病毒(IAV)并补充Clostridium sporogenes的小鼠。研究设计重点在于评估这种细菌干预对疾病严重程度、病毒载量和肺部炎症的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员给小鼠补充Clostridium sporogenes,并评估其对肺部病毒载量、炎症和肠道微生物群组成的影响。他们还测试了IPA及其类似物在基于细胞的实验中的直接抗病毒药物效应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与未治疗的小鼠相比,补充Clostridium sporogenes与较轻的疾病、较低的肺部病毒载量和较少的肺部炎症相关。灭活的C. sporogenes的给药也改善了流感结果,这种效果与系统性IPA水平的恢复相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,C. sporogenes可能调节肠道菌群失调并增强系统性IPA水平,这些水平与疾病严重程度和病毒载量的降低相关,表明其对流感的保护作用可能通过一种新的间接机制实现。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果突显了C. sporogenes作为预防或缓解急性病毒性呼吸道感染的益生菌候选物的潜力,为针对肠道-肺部相互作用的治疗策略提供了新的途径。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于动物模型,IPA的间接效应在流感结果中的作用仍需在人体研究中进一步验证。由于在基于细胞的实验中未观察到直接抗病毒药物效应,因此证据强度中等。

papers.title: Influenza Vaccine Hesitancy and its Associated Factors among Healthcare Workers in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study, 2026
papers.abstract: Background: Seasonal influenza causes substantial morbidity and mortality, and healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of infection and may facilitate healthcare-associated transmission. Although influenza vaccination is freely available and widely promoted in Saudi Arabia, uptake remains suboptimal. This study assessed influenza vaccine hesitancy and its associated factors among HCWs in Saudi Arabia. Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted using a self-administered online questionnaire distributed to HCWs across Saudi Arabia. The survey assessed sociodemographic and professional characteristics, vaccination history and intentions, workplace facilitators, perceived barriers, and hesitancy using an adapted 8-item WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (Cronbach’s alpha=0.91). Hesitancy scores were summarized using the median and interquartile range (IQR). Group differences were examined using Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, and a multivariable generalized linear model was used to identify independently associated factors. Results: A total of 395 HCWs participated. Influenza vaccine uptake during the most recent season was 51.4%, and 54.9% intended to vaccinate in the upcoming season. Workplace accessibility and encouragement were reported by 90.1% and 89.9%, respectively. The most common barriers were fear of side effects (33.7%), perceiving influenza as a mild illness (32.2%), and lack of time (28.1%). The median hesitancy score was 32 (IQR 26–37). Profession was associated with hesitancy in the unadjusted analysis (p=0.042). analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated influenza vaccine hesitancy and its associated factors among healthcare workers in Saudi Arabia. Seasonal influenza is a significant public health concern, with HCWs at higher risk of infection and transmission. The study found that 51.4% of HCWs had been vaccinated in the most recent season, and 54.9% intended to vaccinate in the upcoming season. Common barriers included fear of side effects, perception of influenza as mild, and lack of time. The median hesitancy score was 32 (IQR 26–37), and recent vaccination was the only independently associated factor. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the findings are based on self-reported data, which may introduce bias.

papers.title: Design of NiO/GO Nanocomposites for H1N1 antiviral activity and Molnupiravir Nanocarrier Applications: A Combined Experimental and Theoretical Study
papers.abstract: Pure NiO nanoparticles and nanocomposites NiO/GO at molar ratio of 1:1 NiO:GO were produced using Sol-Gel and comprehensively considered. The structurers and Morphology characterizations revealed that GO incorporation enhanced crystallinity (crystallite size about 11-12 nm) by FESEM, reduced particles agglomeration to 29.8 nm and promoted dispersion on 2D GO sheets. UV.Vis analysis showed improved optical properties, evidenced by band gap narrowing E g (3.4 to 3.0 eV) indicative of enhanced electronic coupling. The FTIR spectrum confirmed robust NiO/GO bonding through C=C and C=O stretches and Photoluminescence (PL) intensity decreased, confirming charge separation. Besides, we the hypothesized that NiO/GO nanocomposite results in synergistic enhancement of electronic properties, antiviral efficacy, and drug-loading capability through improved interfacial interactions, charge separation, and stable molecular adsorption, establishing NiO/GO as a promising multifunctional antiviral activity of pure NiO nanostructure and NiO/GO nanocomposite against H1N1 Influenza A virus using MDCK cells was detected. Furthermore, the cytotoxicity test against MDCK cells indicated no cytotoxic effect for either pure NiO nanostructure or the NiO/GO nanocomposite was detected. In the current study, the theory of density functional (DFT) calculated are approved to explore the adsorption the adsorption behavior and electronic properties of Molnupiravir on a NiO-doped graphene oxide (NiO/GO) nanocomposite. The optimized geometries confirmed the structural stability of the pristine materials and the adsorption complex. The adsorption strength was evaluated using the Boys-Bernardi counterpoise method, yielding a BSSE-corrected interaction energy of -35.77 kcal mol -1 (-1.55 eV), indicating spontaneous and thermodynamically favorable adsorption. To further assess the structural stability of the adsorption system under dynamic conditions, the molecular dynamics simulations were conducted through the Forcite module of Materials Studio, where the energy fluctuations demonstrated that the Molnupiravir/NiO/GO complex remained stable throughout the simulation. The computed band gap of approximately 3.00 eV corroborated the retention of the semiconducting character of the NiO/GO nanocomposite, whereas the density of states (DOS) analysis revealed observable electronic-state redistribution and orbital hybridization during adsorption. Additionally, molecular docking of the optimized Molnupriavir/NiO/GO nanocomposite against the target protein 9NWB resulted in a binding affinity of -9.8 kcal.ml -1 , indicating significant binding via hydrophobic and cooperation of hydrogen-bonding interactions inside the advice site. These findings emphasize NiO/GO nanocomposite potential as a promising nanocarrier for applications of antiviral drug-delivery systems by showing that it offers a robust adsorption platform while preserving Molnupiravir biological activity.

papers.title_original: Design of NiO/GO Nanocomposites for H1N1 antiviral activity and Molnupiravir Nanocarrier Applications: A Combined Experimental and Theoretical Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to design NiO/GO nanocomposites for H1N1 antiviral activity and explore their potential as nanocarriers for drug delivery systems. The background highlights the need for effective antiviral materials against seasonal influenza viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the production of pure NiO nanoparticles and NiO/GO nanocomposites at a 1:1 molar ratio using the Sol-Gel method. The nanocomposites were tested against the H1N1 Influenza A virus using MDCK cells.
analysis.methods: The methods included structural and morphological characterization using FESEM, UV-Vis analysis for optical properties, FTIR for bonding confirmation, and photoluminescence measurements for charge separation. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to assess structural stability and electronic properties.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that GO incorporation enhanced crystallinity, reduced particle agglomeration to 29.8 nm, and promoted dispersion on 2D GO sheets. The band gap narrowed from 3.4 to 3.0 eV, and the adsorption strength was found to be -35.77 kcal mol-1 (-1.55 eV), indicating spontaneous and thermodynamically favorable adsorption. The nanocomposite demonstrated no cytotoxic effect on MDCK cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of the NiO/GO nanocomposite's potential as a multifunctional antiviral material, with synergistic enhancements in electronic properties, antiviral efficacy, and drug-loading capability. This represents a novel approach to antiviral nanocarriers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that NiO/GO nanocomposites could be used as a promising platform for antiviral drug delivery systems, offering a stable and effective adsorption mechanism for drugs like Molnupiravir against H1N1 Influenza A virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analysis using MDCK cells, and the evidence is based on structural, optical, and computational methods without in vivo testing. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the lack of clinical or biological validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the design of NiO/GO nanocomposites for H1N1 antiviral activity and their potential as nanocarriers for drug delivery. The nanocomposites were synthesized using the Sol-Gel method and characterized for structural, optical, and electronic properties. Results indicated enhanced crystallinity, reduced agglomeration, and improved dispersion on GO sheets. The band gap narrowed, and the adsorption strength was found to be thermodynamically favorable. Cytotoxicity tests showed no harmful effects on MDCK cells. The authors hypothesized that the nanocomposite synergistically improves electronic properties, antiviral efficacy, and drug-loading capability. These findings suggest that NiO/GO could serve as a promising antiviral nanocarrier. However, the study is limited to in vitro analysis and computational methods, which may affect the confidence in the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在设计用于H1N1 抗病毒药物活性的NiO/GO纳米复合材料,并探索其作为药物递送系统纳米载体的潜力。背景强调了针对季节性流感病毒开发有效抗病毒药物材料的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及通过溶胶-凝胶法生产纯NiO纳米颗粒和摩尔比为1:1的NiO/GO纳米复合材料。纳米复合材料在MDCK细胞中被测试其对H1N1流感A病毒的活性。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括使用FESEM进行结构和形态表征,通过紫外-可见光谱分析光学性质,利用FTIR确认键合,并通过光致发光测量评估电荷分离。此外,还采用了分子动力学模拟和密度泛函理论(DFT)计算来评估结构稳定性和电子性能。
elements_zh.main_results: The results showed that GO incorporation enhanced crystallinity, reduced particle agglomeration to 29.8 nm, and promoted dispersion on 2D GO sheets. The band gap narrowed from 3.4 to 3.0 eV, and the adsorption strength was found to be -35.77 kcal mol-1 (-1.55 eV), indicating spontaneous and thermodynamically favorable adsorption. The nanocomposite demonstrated no cytotoxic effect on MDCK cells.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为NiO/GO纳米复合材料作为多功能抗病毒药物材料的潜力证据,其在电子性能、抗病毒药物效果和药物负载能力方面表现出协同增强。这代表了一种新型的抗病毒药物纳米载体方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,NiO/GO纳米复合材料可以作为抗病毒药物药物递送系统的有前景平台,为如Molnupiravir等药物提供稳定且有效的吸附机制,以对抗H1N1流感A病毒。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于使用MDCK细胞进行体外分析,证据基于结构、光学和计算方法,而没有进行体内测试。由于缺乏临床或生物学验证,研究结果的可信度中等。

The structurers and Morphology characterizations revealed that GO incorporation enhanced crystallinity (crystallite size about 11-12 nm) by FESEM, reduced particles agglomeration to 29.8 nm and promoted dispersion on 2D GO sheets. UV.Vis analysis showed improved optical properties, evidenced by band gap narrowing E g (3.4 to 3.0 eV) indicative of enhanced electronic coupling. The FTIR spectrum confirmed robust NiO/GO bonding through C=C and C=O stretches and Photoluminescence (PL) intensity decreased, confirming charge separation. Besides, we the hypothesized that NiO/GO nanocomposite results in synergistic enhancement of electronic properties, antiviral efficacy, and drug-loading capability through improved interfacial interactions, charge separation, and stable molecular adsorption, establishing NiO/GO as a promising multifunctional antiviral activity of pure NiO nanostructure and NiO/GO nanocomposite against H1N1 Influenza A virus using MDCK cells was detected. Furthermore, the cytotoxicity test against MDCK cells indicated no cytotoxic effect for either pure NiO nanostructure or the NiO/GO nanocomposite was detected. In the current study, the theory of density functional (DFT) calculated are approved to explore the adsorption the adsorption behavior and electronic properties of Molnupiravir on a NiO-doped graphene oxide (NiO/GO) nanocomposite. The optimized geometries confirmed the structural stability of the pristine materials and the adsorption complex. The adsorption strength was evaluated using the Boys-Bernardi counterpoise method, yielding a BSSE-corrected interaction energy of -35.77 kcal mol -1 (-1.55 eV), indicating spontaneous and thermodynamically favorable adsorption. To further assess the structural stability of the adsorption system under dynamic conditions, the molecular dynamics simulations were conducted through the Forcite module of Materials Studio, where the energy fluctuations demonstrated that the Molnupiravir/NiO/GO complex remained stable throughout the simulation. The computed band gap of approximately 3.00 eV corroborated the retention of the semiconducting character of the NiO/GO nanocomposite, whereas the density of states (DOS) analysis revealed observable electronic-state redistribution and orbital hybridization during adsorption. Additionally, molecular docking of the optimized Molnupriavir/NiO/GO nanocomposite against the target protein 9NWB resulted in a binding affinity of -9.8 kcal.ml -1 , indicating significant binding via hydrophobic and cooperation of hydrogen-bonding interactions inside the advice site. These findings emphasize NiO/GO nanocomposite potential as a promising nanocarrier for applications of antiviral drug-delivery systems by showing that it offers a robust adsorption platform while preserving Molnupiravir biological activity.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在设计用于H1N1 抗病毒药物活性的NiO/GO纳米复合材料,并探索其作为药物递送系统纳米载体的潜力。背景强调了针对季节性流感病毒开发有效抗病毒药物材料的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及通过溶胶-凝胶法生产纯NiO纳米颗粒和摩尔比为1:1的NiO/GO纳米复合材料。纳米复合材料在MDCK细胞中被测试其对H1N1流感A病毒的活性。
analysis_zh.methods: 方法包括使用FESEM进行结构和形态表征,通过紫外-可见光谱分析光学性质,利用FTIR确认键合,并通过光致发光测量评估电荷分离。此外,还采用了分子动力学模拟和密度泛函理论(DFT)计算来评估结构稳定性和电子性能。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为NiO/GO纳米复合材料作为多功能抗病毒药物材料的潜力证据,其在电子性能、抗病毒药物效果和药物负载能力方面表现出协同增强。这代表了一种新型的抗病毒药物纳米载体方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,NiO/GO纳米复合材料可以作为抗病毒药物药物递送系统的有前景平台,为如Molnupiravir等药物提供稳定且有效的吸附机制,以对抗H1N1流感A病毒。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于使用MDCK细胞进行体外分析,证据基于结构、光学和计算方法,而没有进行体内测试。由于缺乏临床或生物学验证,研究结果的可信度中等。

papers.title: Preventive Effect of Cladosiphon okamuranus -Derived Fucoidan against Influenza Virus Infection via Dendritic Cell Activation
papers.abstract: Abstract Fucoidan is a sulfated polysaccharide contained in the viscous components covering the surface of brown algae. We previously revealed that fucoidan derived from Cladosiphon okamuranus (C. okamuranus) cooperatively activates innate immune cells upon stimulation with several pathogen components. Therefore, in this study, the preventive effect of fucoidan against viral infection was evaluated. BALB/c mice were continuously administered 30, 80, or 240 mg/kg of C. okamuranus-derived fucoidan intragastrically for 14 days, subsequently infected with the H1N1 influenza virus. In the control mice, the symptom scores rapidly increased from day 5 postinfection, and all mice died by day 9, whereas in the mice administered 80 mg/kg or more of fucoidan, the symptoms were ameliorated, and death associated with infection was prevented. Viral proliferation in the lungs was significantly suppressed with 80 mg/kg fucoidan during the 3 days postinfection. Furthermore, fucoidan induced an effective antiviral response, characterized by the upregulation of type I and II interferon expression and the accumulation of immune cells. These results clearly demonstrate the efficacy of fucoidan in preventing influenza infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the preventive effect of fucoidan against viral infection, building on prior findings that fucoidan activates innate immune cells when exposed to pathogen components.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved BALB/c mice that were administered 30, 80, or 240 mg/kg of C. okamuranus-derived fucoidan intragastrically for 14 days before being infected with the H1N1 influenza virus.
analysis.methods: The mice were continuously given fucoidan via intragastric administration for 14 days, then infected with the H1N1 influenza virus, and monitored for symptom progression and survival.
analysis.main_results: In the control group, symptom scores increased rapidly from day 5 postinfection, and all mice died by day 9. In contrast, mice administered 80 mg/kg or more of fucoidan showed ameliorated symptoms and no death associated with infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate that fucoidan can effectively prevent influenza infection by reducing symptoms and mortality, highlighting its potential as a preventive agent.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that fucoidan could be a valuable supplement in preventing influenza infection, particularly in populations at risk of severe outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to animal models, and the evidence is based on an abstract-only report, which may not fully capture the complexity of human influenza infection. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the preventive effect of fucoidan derived from Cladosiphon okamuranus against influenza virus infection. The research builds on prior findings that fucoidan activates innate immune cells when exposed to pathogen components. BALB/c mice were administered 30, 80, or 240 mg/kg of fucoidan intragastrically for 14 days before being infected with the H1N1 influenza virus. papers.title_zh: 源于海带的岩藻多糖对流感病毒感染的预防作用:通过树突状细胞激活
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Fucoidan is a sulfated polysaccharide contained in the viscous components covering the surface of brown algae. We previously revealed that fucoidan derived from Cladosiphon okamuranus (C. okamuranus) cooperatively activates innate immune cells upon stimulation with several pathogen components. Therefore, in this study, the preventive effect of fucoidan against viral infection was evaluated. BALB/c mice were continuously administered 30, 80, or 240 mg/kg of C. okamuranus-derived fucoidan intragastrically for 14 days, subsequently infected with the H1N1 influenza virus. In the control mice, the symptom scores rapidly increased from day 5 postinfection, and all mice died by day 9, whereas in the mice administered 80 mg/kg or more of fucoidan, the symptoms were ameliorated, and death associated with infection was prevented. Viral proliferation in the lungs was significantly suppressed with 80 mg/kg fucoidan during the 3 days postinfection. Furthermore, fucoidan induced an effective antiviral response, characterized by the upregulation of type I and II interferon expression and the accumulation of immune cells. These results clearly demonstrate the efficacy of fucoidan in preventing influenza infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 岩藻多糖是一种存在于褐藻表面粘液成分中的硫酸化多糖。我们之前发现,源于Cladosiphon okamuranus(C. okamuranus)的岩藻多糖在与多种病原体成分刺激时,能够协同激活先天免疫细胞。因此,在本研究中,评估了岩藻多糖对病毒感染的预防作用。将BALB/c小鼠连续14天通过胃内给药给予30、80或240 mg/kg的C. okamuranus来源的岩藻多糖,随后感染H1N1流感病毒。在对照组小鼠中,感染后第5天症状评分迅速上升,所有小鼠在第9天均死亡,而在给予80 mg/kg或更高剂量岩藻多糖的小鼠中,症状得到缓解,且感染相关死亡被预防。感染后3天内,肺部病毒增殖在80 mg/kg剂量的岩藻多糖作用下显著受到抑制。此外,岩藻多糖诱导了有效的免疫应答,表现为I型和II型干扰素表达的上调以及免疫细胞的聚集。这些结果清楚地表明,岩藻多糖在预防流感感染方面具有显著效果。

news.content: This publication is licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated. To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk . Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-reports-2026-to-2027-season/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-report-12-november-2026-week-46 This report summarises the information from the surveillance systems which are used to monitor COVID-19 (caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)), influenza, respiratory syncytial virus ( RSV ) and diseases caused by other seasonal respiratory viruses in England. The report is based on data up to week 45 of 2026 (2 November to 8 November 2026). The main messages of this report are: Annual reports for the 2025 to 2026 season: Influenza in the UK, annual epidemiological report: winter 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Epidemiology of COVID-19 in England (published 25 June 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in all GP patients: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in school-aged children: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in frontline healthcare workers: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Influenza activity increased and is circulating at low levels. Emergency department ( ED ) attendances for influenza-like-illness ( ILI ) increased and were above seasonally expected levels. The number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection ( ARI ) incidents increased compared with the previous week. A briefing note has been issued to inform the NHS that influenza activity is now above baseline levels. Compared with the equivalent week last season (week 45 data, 2025 to 2026), vaccine uptake is lower among patients aged 65 years and over (63.1% versus 65.1%), patients aged 6 months to under 65 years in clinical risk groups (30.4% versus 31.4%), those aged 2 years (35.8% versus 36.6%), and those aged 3 years (35.6% versus 36.8%). In contrast, vaccine uptake is higher among pregnant women (32.7% versus 31.4%). Influenza vaccination data was unavailable or incomplete at the time of analysis in weeks 41 and 42 and led to several cohorts not being published in week 42. This has been corrected since week 43, and all cohorts are included. This will be corrected retrospectively in the report for week 42. There remains an issue that affects the attribution of vaccinations by provider setting. This is not expected to affect overall vaccination uptake estimates, which are considered to remain an accurate reflection of the influenza vaccination programme. COVID-19 activity was stable and is circulating at low levels. ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness decreased. The number of COVID-19 confirmed acute respiratory infections ( ARI ) incidents increased compared with the previous week. By the end of week 45 2026, 51.8% of all people aged 75 years and over in England had been vaccinated with an autumn 2026 dose. Similarly, 22.1% of all people aged under 75 years with a weakened immune system in England had been vaccinated with an autumn 2026 dose since 1 October 2026. RSV hospital activity increased to low levels with other indicators within baseline levels. ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis increased and were below seasonally expected levels. Note 1: these indicators use the moving epidemic method ( MEM ) and the mean standard deviation method ( MSD ) to define thresholds to determine their respective levels of activity. Further information on these methods can be found in Influenza surveillance in Europe: establishing epidemic thresholds by the Moving Epidemic Method and Setting thresholds to determine COVID-19 activity levels using the mean standard deviation ( MSD ) method, England, 2022 to 2024 . The MEM approach is well-established for some influenza surveillance indicators, however, for other indicators both the MEM and MSD are experimental and may be subject to future revision. Influenza laboratory surveillance and GP swabbing positivity have transitioned from using MEM to using MSD . These approaches will be considered alongside expert opinion and triangulation of other data sources. The Second Generation Surveillance System ( SGSS ) captures test result information for notifiable infectious diseases, including COVID-19 and influenza, from laboratories in England. The unified sample dataset ( USD ) stores all SARS-CoV-2 test results reported to SGSS , Respiratory DataMart and UKHSA laboratories, and is used to calculate the percentage of tests positive for SARS-CoV-2 among all SARS-CoV-2 tests conducted. As of 10 November 2026, there were a total of 1,587 COVID-19 cases identified in hospital settings in week 45, decreasing from 1,914 cases in the previous week. SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) PCR positivity in hospital settings remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 7.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026 compared with 7.4% for the same period on the previous Sunday. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 10.7% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This has remained stable compared to 10.7% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Note 2: data from previous seasons is aligned by day. Note 3: testing policy and practice may change over time which can impact positivity rates, therefore comparisons over time should be interpreted with caution. Notable changes in testing policy occurred during 2022 to 2023, which are outlined in the data quality report . Note 4: the highlighted line corresponds to the age group in the subplot title, grey lines correspond to all other age groups. Influenza positivity remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 8.1% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This is compared with 7.8% on the previous Sunday. By type, influenza A positivity remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 7.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. Influenza B positivity remained stable in the same week, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 0.3% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. Influenza A positivity rates were highest among those aged between 5 and 11 years, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 12.8% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This has increased from 10.7% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Influenza B positivity rates for the same period were highest among those aged between 12 and 17 years, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 1.6%. This has increased from 1.0% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. RSV swab-positivity based PCR test results reported through SGSS have been included as a pilot indicator from week 49 2025 onwards. RSV positivity increased in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 3.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026, compared with 2.5% up to the previous Sunday. RSV positivity rates were highest in those aged between 0 and 4 years with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 19.6% up to Sunday 8 November 2026 in week 45. This has increased from 15.6% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Respiratory DataMart is a sentinel laboratory-based surveillance system where participating laboratories report positive and negative test results for a number of respiratory viruses from samples primarily taken in hospital. A small proportion of primary care samples are also included in this reporting. In week 45, data is based on reporting from 9 out of the 14 sentinel laboratories. In week 45, 4,231 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for influenza. There were 328 positive samples for influenza: 216 influenza A (not subtyped), 10 influenza A (H3N2), 88 influenza A (H1N1)pdm09, and 18 influenza B. Overall, influenza positivity remained stable at 7.8% in week 45 compared with 7.5% in the previous week. In week 45, 4,588 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for SARS-CoV-2. There were 271 positive samples for SARS-CoV-2. SARS-CoV-2 positivity decreased slightly to 5.9% compared with 7.2% in the previous week, with the highest positivity in those aged 80 years and over at 9.4%. RSV positivity increased slightly to 3.2%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 17.5%. Adenovirus positivity remained stable at 1.8%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 5 and 14 years at 5.6%. Human metapneumovirus ( hMPV ) positivity decreased to 0.1%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 65 and 79 years at 0.3%. Parainfluenza positivity remained stable at 3.6%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 11.7%. Rhinovirus positivity decreased slightly to 14.1%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 28.4%. DataMart data is provisional and subject to retrospective updates. Note 5: shading represents 95% confidence intervals. This section is updated fortnightly. Data below was last updated in the week 45 report. UKHSA conducts genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 lineages. This section provides an overview of circulating lineages in England, derived from data on sequenced PCR -positive SARS-CoV-2 samples in SGSS . The prevalence of UKHSA -designated lineages among sequenced cases is presented in Figure 13. To account for reporting delays, we report the proportion of lineages within COVID-19 cases that have had a sequenced positive sample between 28 September 2026 and 11 October 2026. Note that low sequencing numbers, especially within the latest reporting period, will impact the accuracy of the prevalence estimates. These most recent figures should therefore be interpreted with caution. Note that lineages will be grouped independently from their parent lineage once they reach sufficient prevalence, and may be re-grouped into their parent lineage if their prevalence subsequently falls. The data quality report contains more information on lineage groupings. Analysis of viruses from primary and secondary care shows that circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses show low genetic diversity and all belong to clade D.3.1.1. Observations published from the WHO influenza vaccine composition meeting (VCM) in September 2026 suggest low reactivity of some viruses within the D.3.1.1 subclade with post-infection ferret antisera raised against A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like virus – the A(H1N1)pdm09 component in 2026 Southern and 2026 to 2027 Northern Hemisphere cell- and egg-based influenza vaccines - and human sera post-vaccination with the Southern Hemisphere vaccine 2026. It is not yet clear how vaccine effectiveness against clinical disease may be affected by these observations. Vaccines typically still provide protection against severe clinical disease when drifted strains are seen with only a modest reduction in effectiveness. The characterisation of circulating A(H3N2) viruses shows that A(H3N2) viruses are currently showing low genetic diversity. All sequenced viruses to date belong to genetic subclade K. To date, only a small number of influenza B viruses have been detected, which show some genetic diversity. Between week 35 2026 (week ending 30 August 2026) and week 45 2026 (week ending 8 November 2026), the UKHSA respiratory virus unit ( RVU ) has genetically characterised 397 seasonal influenza viruses, and identified 267 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses, 96 influenza A(H3N2) viruses, and 34 influenza B viruses. Details of the characterised viruses by subtype are shown in Tables 1, 2 and 3. The RVU has confirmed by genome sequencing the detection of live attenuated influenza vaccine ( LAIV ) viruses in 16 influenza A/B positive samples, collected from children aged between 2 and 16 years. UKHSA RVU performs antigenic characterisation of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, influenza A(H3N2) and influenza B viruses using haemagglutination inhibition ( HI ) assays. Data from these assays are used to compare how similar the currently circulating influenza viruses are to the strains included in seasonal influenza vaccines, and to monitor for changes in circulating influenza viruses. Similarity of currently circulating influenza strains to vaccine strains is defined as having an antibody titre within 4-fold when compared with reference viruses representative of the vaccine strain. Antigenic characterisation of viruses in the current reporting period is underway. A(H1N1)pdm09: 13 A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses have been antigenically characterised and 11 were similar to reference viruses representative of the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like Northern Hemisphere 2026 to 2027 (H1N1)pdm09 vaccine strains. A(H3N2): 6 A(H3N2) viruses have been antigenically characterised and 6 were similar to reference viruses representative of the A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2)-like and A/Darwin/1415/2025 (H3N2)-like Northern Hemisphere 2026 to 2027 (H3N2) vaccine strains. Influenza positive samples are screened for mutations in the virus neuraminidase ( NA ) and the cap-dependent endonuclease of the polymerase acidic protein (PA) genes known to confer neuraminidase inhibitor (oseltamivir and zanamivir) or baloxavir resistance, respectively. Results from this surveillance are given in table 4. There have been seven detections with mutations related to reduced susceptibility/resistance to oseltamivir and/or reduced susceptibility to baloxavir. Data is presented on viral ARI incidents in different settings that are reported to UKHSA health protection teams ( HPTs ). Please note that reporting practices are known to vary between seasons and between regions. Any interpretation of temporal and regional trends should consider the likelihood of differences in reporting of ARI incidents over time and between regions. There were 124 new ARI incidents reported in week 45 in England. These included: 114 incidents from care homes, of which 25 were due to SARS-CoV-2, 23 were due to influenza A, 12 were due to influenza (no type information available), 5 were due to multiple pathogens, 4 were due to other pathogens and 1 was due to RSV . No pathogen was reported in 44 incidents 2 incidents from hospitals, of which 2 were due to SARS-CoV-2 7 incidents from educational settings, of which 3 were due to RSV and 1 was due to influenza (no type information available). No pathogen was reported in 3 incidents 1 incident from other settings, of which 1 was due to SARS-CoV-2 FluSurvey is an internet-based participatory surveillance system based on the InfluenzaNet platform. It monitors trends of influenza-like illness ( ILI ) in the community using self-reported respiratory symptoms from registered participants. As a participatory surveillance system, new signups can occur throughout the season and participation can vary in each week. The European Centre for Disease Control ( ECDC ) ILI case definition of sudden onset of symptoms with at least one of fever (chills), malaise, headache, muscle pain and at least one of cough, sore throat, shortness of breath is used for reporting. Please note that ILI is a broad definition and can include other respiratory illnesses such as COVID-19. Healthcare use is presented as self-reported use of health services among participants meeting the ILI ECDC case definition. Where a person reports use of more than one healthcare service, secondary care will be indicated over primary care use and physical attendance to primary care will be indicated over use of remote services (for example, online NHS services, telephoning their GP or 111). During week commencing 2 November 2026: there were 2,484 participants who completed the weekly symptoms questionnaire 361 (14.5%) reported fever or cough and 126 (5.1%) met the ILI case definition, in the past week 14.3% of participants meeting the ILI case definition reported contact with healthcare services as a result of self-reported symptoms; the most frequently reported contact was a visit to the pharmacy the proportion of participants meeting the ILI case definition slightly decreased compared with the previous week (5.1% compared with 5.3% in week 44) data submitted in the current week (commencing 9 November) is available on the UKHSA data dashboard to support more timely insights. For further details see the data quality report Syndromic surveillance collects data from various healthcare sources where presentations are classified by patterns of symptoms compatible with specific infections. In some settings, the syndromic diagnosis can be supplemented by (rapid) testing. In this report, ED attendances are displayed. Further details and data from other syndromic surveillance systems can be found in the syndromic surveillance weekly summaries . During the week ending on 8 November 2026, ED attendances for acute respiratory infections increased slightly and were similar to the seasonally expected level. ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness decreased. ED attendance for influenza-like illness increased slightly and was above seasonally expected levels. ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis (a syndrome related to RSV infection) increased and were below seasonally expected levels. NHS 111 online assessments for acute respiratory infections increased and remained similar to expected levels, while NHS 111 triaged calls for acute respiratory infections remained stable and below expected levels. GP in-hours consultation rates for lower respiratory tract infections and bronchiolitis increased in children aged 0 to 4 years. Though consultation rates for upper respiratory tract infections remained stable overall, consultation rates for influenza-like illness increased slightl…

Note 4: the highlighted line corresponds to the age group in the subplot title, grey lines correspond to all other age groups. Influenza positivity remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 8.1% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This is compared with 7.8% on the previous Sunday. analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 12 November 2026 (week 46) highlights that influenza activity in England has increased and is circulating at low levels. Emergency department attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) have risen above seasonally expected levels, and the number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents has increased compared to the previous week. The report also notes that vaccine uptake among certain groups, such as those aged 65 and over, is lower than the previous season. While influenza laboratory surveillance and GP swabbing positivity have transitioned from using the Moving Epidemic Method (MEM) to the Mean Standard Deviation Method (MSD), data for weeks 41 and 42 was incomplete, but this has been corrected since week 43. The report emphasizes that the methods used for defining activity levels are experimental and may be subject to future revision. Additionally, it mentions that the Second Generation Surveillance System (SGSS) captures test results for influenza and other respiratory viruses, and the unified sample dataset (USD) is used to calculate positivity rates for SARS-CoV-2. Overall, the report provides an updated overview of influenza and related respiratory virus activity in England, with a focus on monitoring and data collection methods.

news.title: Hospitalized influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates in Shiraz lack major antiviral resistance mutations
news.excerpt: An observational study of hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, found neuraminidase genetic variability but no established antiviral resistance mutations among influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, November 17, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Hospitalized influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates in Shiraz lack major antiviral resistance mutations by November 15, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Hospitalized influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates in Shiraz lack major antiviral resistance mutations Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram An observational study investigating influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses recovered from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, between November 2023 and December 2024 revealed ongoing genomic variability in the viral neuraminidase gene but found no evidence of established resistance-associated mutations to standard neuraminidase inhibitor therapeutics. Researchers evaluated respiratory specimens from individuals presenting with acute respiratory infections to track how the circulating pathogen has evolved relative to the founding pandemic lineage. The investigation focused on determining whether mutations in the neuraminidase surface glycoprotein might compromise the inhibitory effectiveness of widely utilized antiviral drugs, including oseltamivir and zanamivir. Although the sequenced isolates displayed multiple amino acid substitutions across the neuraminidase gene, none carried the major recognized genetic markers that confer reduced drug sensitivity. The study contextualizes these genomic observations within the broader evolutionary history of the pathogen, noting that the 2009 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pandemic caused substantial morbidity and mortality on a global scale. In the years following its initial emergence, continuous molecular surveillance has remained essential because structural changes in the viral neuraminidase gene can alter multiple biological properties. Specifically, amino acid mutations within this gene may influence the ongoing evolution of the virus, facilitate immune evasion against host defenses, and modify viral susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors. To assess the molecular characteristics of circulating strains during the 2023–2024 season, the authors conducted an observational surveillance protocol involving patients admitted with acute respiratory infections in Shiraz. Between November 2023 and December 2024, the team collected a total of 300 respiratory samples across the hospitalized cohort. Each specimen was systematically screened for the presence of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays. From this initial diagnostic screening of 300 clinical samples, the researchers identified fourteen specimens that tested positive for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, providing the defined sample set for comprehensive downstream molecular and computational characterization. The fourteen confirmed positive isolates subsequently underwent full-length neuraminidase gene sequencing to identify all coding changes present across the complete viral gene. In addition to amino acid substitution analysis, the researchers conducted phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and computational molecular docking to evaluate how the observed sequence variations might affect viral protein structure and drug interactions. For phylogenetic comparison, the investigators utilized the historical pandemic reference strain designated A/California/07/2009 (GenBank accession NC_026434.1). Comparing the newly isolated Iranian sequences directly against this reference strain allowed the authors to measure the extent of neuraminidase sequence divergence that has accumulated relative to the founding A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage. Detailed sequence analysis of the fourteen isolates uncovered eighteen distinct amino acid substitutions distributed across the neuraminidase gene. The two most prevalent substitutions detected in the cohort were V241I and N369K, each occurring in 13 of the 14 isolates, representing a frequency of 92.9 percent. The researchers noted that V241I and N369K are consistent with previously documented lineage-associated permissive substitutions that commonly circulate in modern A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. Among the other identified changes, the N200S substitution appeared in 4 of the 14 isolates (28.6 percent), while the V394I substitution was observed in 2 of the 14 isolates (14.3 percent). Additionally, the analysis identified the N386K substitution, which has been previously associated with the alteration of an N-linked glycosylation site on the neuraminidase protein. A central objective of the genomic evaluation was screening the fourteen neuraminidase sequences for established resistance-associated substitutions recognized by the World Health Organization. This targeted screening revealed that none of the isolates harbored major known neuraminidase inhibitor resistance markers, confirming the complete absence of the classic H275Y substitution as well as the I223V substitution. To supplement the sequence-level screening, the researchers carried out structural modeling and computational molecular docking with the antiviral agents oseltamivir and zanamivir. The docking simulations indicated preserved predicted binding of both oseltamivir and zanamivir to the viral neuraminidase active site, reinforcing the genetic findings that the analyzed viral variants maintain predicted susceptibility to these therapeutic agents. The authors concluded that while influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses isolated from hospitalized patients in Shiraz during the 2023–2024 period exhibited measurable genetic variability in the neuraminidase gene, they completely lacked established neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated substitutions. The sequence-based evidence confirms the absence of established resistance markers among the fourteen analyzed clinical isolates, suggesting that standard antiviral therapies retained their molecular targets during the study window. However, because this investigation was strictly observational and did not evaluate clinical trial outcomes or patient treatment responses, the researchers emphasized the necessity of continued molecular surveillance to monitor for the potential emergence of clinically relevant neuraminidase mutations in circulating populations. analysis.time: The study was conducted between November 2023 and December 2024, with the report published on November 15, 2026 (N1).
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, with a total of 300 respiratory samples collected (N9).
analysis.event: An observational study investigated influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates from hospitalized patients in Shiraz, Iran, between November 2023 and December 2024, revealing genomic variability but no major antiviral resistance mutations (N1).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study identified 14 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates from 300 samples, with 18 distinct amino acid substitutions across the neuraminidase gene. None of the isolates carried major resistance markers like H275Y or I223V (N11, N16, N22).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study involved full-length neuraminidase gene sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, structural modeling, and molecular docking to assess antiviral susceptibility. The findings suggest that standard antiviral therapies remain effective against the analyzed isolates (N12, N13, N24).

analysis.brief_en: A study conducted between November 2023 and December 2024 in Shiraz, Iran, analyzed influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates from hospitalized patients. Researchers collected 300 respiratory samples and identified 14 positive cases for further molecular analysis. The investigation revealed multiple amino acid substitutions in the neuraminidase gene, including V241I and N369K, which were prevalent in 92.9% of isolates. However, none of the isolates carried major resistance markers such as H275Y or I223V, which are known to reduce susceptibility to antiviral drugs like oseltamivir and zanamivir. The study also performed structural modeling and molecular docking to confirm that the analyzed variants maintain predicted binding to these therapeutic agents. These findings suggest that standard antiviral treatments remain effective against the circulating influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strains in Shiraz during the study period. The research highlights the importance of continuous molecular surveillance to monitor potential changes in viral properties that could affect drug efficacy.

news.title_zh: 设拉子住院流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 分离株缺乏主要 抗病毒药物 耐药性 突变
news.source_body_en: A study conducted between November 2023 and December 2024 in Shiraz, Iran, analyzed influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates from hospitalized patients. Researchers collected 300 respiratory samples and identified 14 positive cases for further molecular analysis. The investigation revealed multiple amino acid substitutions in the neuraminidase gene, including V241I and N369K, which were prevalent in 92.9% of isolates. However, none of the isolates carried major resistance markers such as H275Y or I223V, which are known to reduce susceptibility to antiviral drugs like oseltamivir and zanamivir. The study also performed structural modeling and molecular docking to confirm that the analyzed variants maintain predicted binding to these therapeutic agents. These findings suggest that standard antiviral treatments remain effective against the circulating influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 strains in Shiraz during the study period. The research highlights the importance of continuous molecular surveillance to monitor potential changes in viral properties that could affect drug efficacy.
news.content_zh: 一项于2023年11月至2024年12月在伊朗设拉子进行的研究分析了住院患者中的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 分离株。研究人员收集了300份呼吸道样本,并确定了14例阳性病例以进行进一步的分子分析。调查发现神经氨酸酶基因中存在多种氨基酸替换,包括V241I和N369K,这些替换在92.9%的分离株中普遍存在。然而,这些分离株中均未发现主要耐药性标记,如H275Y或I223V,这些标记已知会降低对抗病毒药物药物如奥司他韦和扎那米韦的敏感性。该研究还通过结构建模和分子对接确认了所分析的变异体仍能预测性地结合这些治疗药物。这些结果表明,在研究期间,标准抗病毒药物治疗方案对设拉子地区流行的流感 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 株仍有效。该研究强调了持续进行基因组监测的重要性,以跟踪可能影响药物疗效的病毒特性变化。

news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Medical Contracting seasonal flu increases the risk of heart attack and stroke. Seasonal influenza is not simply a respiratory infection; it can also increase the risk of heart attack and stroke, especially in the elderly and those with underlying health conditions. Báo Đầu tư•13/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Seasonal influenza typically causes fever, cough, sore throat, headache, and fatigue. Most people recover after a period of rest and appropriate treatment. However, for the elderly, those with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or chronic lung disease, influenza infection can lead to serious, even life-threatening, complications. Get Cold Relief Experts warn that cardiovascular events can occur in the early days of flu infection, even in people who have never been diagnosed with heart disease. According to Associate Professor Dr. Tran Song Giang, Deputy Director of the Cardiovascular Institute, Bach Mai Hospital, when the influenza virus enters the body, an inflammatory response is activated, leading to changes in blood clotting and increasing the burden on the cardiovascular system. Get Cold Relief Notably, the inflammatory response can make atherosclerotic plaques in the arteries less stable and more prone to rupture. This process facilitates the formation of blood clots, causing blockages in blood flow. If this occurs in the coronary arteries, the patient is at risk of myocardial infarction; if it occurs in the cerebral blood vessels, it can lead to ischemic stroke. In addition, influenza infection puts more strain on the heart. When a person has a fever or infection, their heart rate increases, leading to increased oxygen demand from the heart muscle. Conversely, if the flu causes pneumonia or respiratory failure, the amount of oxygen supplied to the body decreases. An imbalance between oxygen demand and supply can increase the risk of myocardial ischemia and worsen pre-existing heart failure. In some cases, direct damage to the myocardium due to the virus may also occur. Associate Professor Tran Song Giang noted that these complications do not only occur in people who have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. Even people who have never been diagnosed with heart disease before can still experience complications when infected with influenza. Studies cited by experts show that influenza infection is associated with a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular events, especially in the early stages of the illness. Get Cold Relief Some studies have noted that the risk of heart attack may increase 6-10 times, while the risk of stroke may increase 3-10 times after contracting the flu. These are relative increases in risk observed in specific studies and do not mean that all people with the flu will experience complications. The elderly are a group that requires particular caution. According to data presented at the conference, people aged 65 and older account for approximately 70% of hospitalizations due to seasonal influenza and 85% of influenza-related deaths in the statistics cited. For individuals with underlying conditions such as hypertension, coronary artery disease, heart failure, diabetes, chronic lung disease, or chronic kidney disease, influenza can worsen their health, especially if these conditions are not well controlled. Notably, some patients have developed severe pneumonia, with lung damage significantly affecting gas exchange capacity, requiring respiratory support with oxygen concentrations of approximately 40-50% to maintain blood oxygenation. When flu symptoms appear, patients need to closely monitor their health, especially those at high risk. Get Cold Relief According to experts, seasonal influenza not only affects the respiratory system but can also have serious impacts on the cardiovascular system. Proactive vaccination, managing underlying medical conditions, and early recognition of dangerous signs are crucial factors in reducing the risk of heart attack, stroke, and other life-threatening complications. Therefore, people should proactively get vaccinated before the flu season or as soon as conditions permit, instead of waiting until the number of cases increases before getting vaccinated. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, November 17, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Single amino acid change broadens influenza B mRNA vaccine protection by November 14, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Single amino acid change broadens influenza B mRNA vaccine protection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers at the National Institutes for Drug Control in Beijing have demonstrated that a single amino acid substitution in the hemagglutinin protein of an influenza B vaccine candidate significantly broadens its protective capacity in mice. Published in Frontiers in Microbiology, the study details how introducing a D212N mutation into the B/Austria/1359417/2021 (BV21) strain restores a specific glycosylation motif, thereby enhancing cross-neutralizing antibody responses against diverse subclades of the B/Victoria lineage. This minimal antigenic modification addresses a critical limitation in current seasonal influenza B vaccination, where the WHO-recommended BV21 strain lacks a glycosylation position that is associated with broader cross-protection. The study was motivated by the observation that no naturally circulating B/Yamagata-lineage viruses have been confirmed since March 2020, making protection against the B/Victoria (BV) lineage the primary focus of influenza B vaccine development. Previous work by the same team identified that the T214A mutation in the hemagglutinin protein significantly alters cross-neutralization capacity, potentially through changes in glycosylation patterns. However, the BV21 strain, which is currently recommended by the World Health Organization, possesses a threonine at position 214 but differs from the broadly reactive B/Wyoming/06/2014 (BW06) strain at position 212, where it contains an aspartic acid (D) instead of an asparagine (N). The research team hypothesized that this D212N difference might influence glycosylation and, consequently, the breadth of the antibody response elicited by the vaccine. To test this hypothesis, the researchers utilized an mRNA platform to compare the cross-subclade protection provided by the BW06 and BV21 strains within the B/Victoria lineage. They synthesized nucleotide-modified mRNAs encoding the hemagglutinin proteins of these strains and encapsulated them in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) using an SM-103-based lipid formulation. The team also introduced the D212N substitution into the BV21 background to create a modified vaccine candidate. Quality control of the mRNA-LNP formulations, including particle size, polydispersity index, and encapsulation efficiency, was assessed to ensure consistency across the experimental groups. The immunogenicity of these vaccines was evaluated in female BALB/c mice, which were randomly assigned to vaccine and control groups. The mice received intramuscular injections of the mRNA vaccines, followed by a booster dose after 21 days. Serum samples collected after the booster immunization were tested in pseudovirus neutralization assays to measure cross-neutralizing activity against representative influenza B strains from distinct subclades in the GISAID database. The results showed that while BV21 induced robust neutralization against its homologous V1A.3a.2 subclade, it exhibited weaker activity against other subclades within the B/Victoria lineage. In contrast, the BW06 strain consistently outperformed BV21 in neutralizing heterologous subclades, highlighting its broader and more balanced cross-protective potential. The introduction of the D212N substitution into the BV21 background resulted in a marked increase in neutralizing antibody titers against heterologous strains. Mass spectrometry analysis confirmed the presence of glycosylation at the D212N mutation position, supporting the hypothesis that the restored glycosylation motif contributed to the enhanced immune response. When the ID50 values for heterologous pseudoviruses were normalized to those of the homologous strains, the D212N-modified vaccine demonstrated a more balanced and consistent cross-neutralizing profile than the original BV21 strain. This suggests that the minimal antigenic modification effectively broadens the scope of protection without compromising the antigenic integrity of the vaccine. To assess in vivo protective efficacy, the researchers performed viral challenge experiments with multiple influenza B strains, including B/Brisbane/60/2008, B/Washington/02/2019, and B/Austria/1359417/2021. Mice were challenged intranasally with five times the median lethal dose (LD50) of these viruses 35 days after booster immunization. A quadrivalent influenza vaccine (QIV) was included as a reference control to benchmark the performance of the mRNA vaccines. Body weight and survival were monitored for 14 days following the challenge, with mice that lost more than 25% of their initial body weight being humanely euthanized. The challenge experiments revealed significant differences in protective efficacy among the vaccine groups. Following challenge with B/Brisbane/2008, all mice in the negative control group succumbed by day 6, whereas both low- and high-dose BW06 and BV21 groups exhibited 100% survival. However, when challenged with B/Washington/02/2019, the original BV21 groups showed only 62.5% survival, while the high-dose BW06 group achieved 100% survival. The D212N-modified vaccine demonstrated superior protection in this scenario, with the high-dose group achieving 100% survival, surpassing the original BV21. Across all tested challenge strains, high-dose D212N immunization resulted in 100% survival, indicating a substantial improvement in cross-lineage protection. Pulmonary viral loads and histopathological changes were also evaluated to further characterize the vaccine-mediated protection. On day 4 or 8 post-challenge, lung tissues were collected and analyzed for viral RNA levels using RT-PCR and for pathological changes using hematoxylin and eosin staining. The negative control groups consistently showed significantly higher viral loads and more severe histopathological changes compared to the vaccinated groups. These findings are consistent with the observed protection in terms of body weight maintenance and survival rates. The study also investigated the temporal distribution of amino acid residues at position 212 in influenza B virus hemagglutinin sequences deposited in the GISAID database through 2026. The analysis revealed that the N212 residue was highly prevalent among earlier circulating strains but declined markedly after 2020, accompanied by an increase in D212 and subsequently E212 variants. Notably, despite the predominance of E212 during 2022–2024, the proportion of N212 increased again after 2024, indicating its renewed representation among recently sampled strains. This dynamic variation at HA position 212, which is located within the 190-helix, a major antigenic region of the hemagglutinin protein, underscores the continued relevance of N212 in the evolutionary landscape of influenza B viruses. Despite the promising results, the authors acknowledge several limitations in the study. The evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity was conducted at matched mRNA doses, and cell-based assays were used to confirm antigen expression, but these comparisons do not isolate the potential contributions of differences in antigen abundance or trimer stability. Furthermore, because the D212N substitution changes both the amino acid side chain and the glycosylation status, the specific contribution of the added glycan to the enhanced breadth remains unresolved. The study also did not determine whether the increased breadth involved altered epitope targeting, and the potential involvement of germinal center competition or mannose-binding lectin-mediated antigen clearance remains hypothetical. The findings provide valuable insights for the development of broadly protective influenza B vaccines, particularly in the context of the ongoing threat posed by the rapid antigenic evolution of influenza viruses. The WHO annually recommends vaccine strains for the Southern and Northern Hemispheres, but vaccine-strain mismatches are common due to this rapid evolution. The ability to rapidly adapt mRNA vaccine production to emerging viral strains offers a significant advantage over traditional peptide- or DNA-based platforms. The D212N-modified BV21 mRNA vaccine represents a step toward next-generation vaccines that can provide broader cross-protection against diverse influenza variants. Future studies incorporating ferret models and sera from individuals with prior influenza infection or vaccination could further assess the antigenic breadth and the influence of pre-existing immunity on the vaccine response. The renewed increase in the proportion of N212 after 2024 highlights the importance of monitoring the prevalence of viral strains and adapting vaccine strategies accordingly. These findings support further exploration of glycosylation-site engineering as a strategy to broaden influenza B vaccine protection, potentially leading to more effective and durable seasonal influenza vaccines in the future. The evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity was conducted at matched mRNA doses, and cell-based assays were used to confirm antigen expression, but these comparisons do not isolate the potential contributions of differences in antigen abundance or trimer stability. Furthermore, because the D212N substitution changes both the amino acid side chain and the glycosylation status, the specific contribution of the added glycan to the enhanced breadth remains unresolved. The study also did not determine whether the increased breadth involved altered epitope targeting, and the potential involvement of germinal center competition or mannose-binding lectin-mediated antigen clearance remains hypothetical. The findings provide valuable insights for the development of broadly protective influenza B vaccines, particularly in the context of the ongoing threat posed by the rapid antigenic evolution of influenza viruses. The WHO annually recommends vaccine strains for the Southern and Northern Hemispheres, but vaccine-strain mismatches are common due to this rapid evolution. The ability to rapidly adapt mRNA vaccine production to emerging viral strains offers a significant advantage over traditional peptide- or DNA-based platforms. The D212N-modified BV21 mRNA vaccine represents a step toward next-generation vaccines that can provide broader cross-protection against diverse influenza variants. Future studies incorporating ferret models and sera from individuals with prior influenza infection or vaccination could further assess the antigenic breadth and the influence of pre-existing immunity on the vaccine response. The renewed increase in the proportion of N212 after 2024 highlights the importance of monitoring the prevalence of viral strains and adapting vaccine strategies accordingly. These findings support further exploration of glycosylation-site engineering as a strategy to broaden influenza B vaccine protection, potentially leading to more effective and durable seasonal influenza vaccines in the future. analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 14, 2026, by researchers at the National Institutes for Drug Control in Beijing explored a potential enhancement in influenza B vaccine protection. The research focused on the B/Victoria lineage, where the World Health Organization-recommended strain BV21 lacks a glycosylation position linked to broader cross-protection. By introducing a D212N mutation into the hemagglutinin protein of BV21, the team created a modified vaccine candidate that demonstrated improved cross-neutralizing antibody responses against diverse subclades of the B/Victoria lineage. The study used an mRNA platform and tested the vaccines in female BALB/c mice, with results showing that the D212N-modified vaccine achieved 100% survival in challenge experiments against multiple influenza B strains, surpassing the original BV21 strain. The findings suggest that this minimal antigenic modification could broaden vaccine protection without compromising its antigenic integrity. Future studies are planned to assess the vaccine's performance in ferret models and with human sera to evaluate its antigenic breadth and the influence of pre-existing immunity.

news.content_zh: 一项由北京国家药物控制研究所研究人员于2026年11月14日发表的研究探讨了流感B病毒疫苗保护潜力的增强。该研究聚焦于B/Victoria谱系,其中世界卫生组织推荐的毒株BV21缺乏与广泛交叉保护相关的糖基化位点。通过在BV21的血凝素蛋白中引入D212N 突变突变,研究团队创建了一种改良的疫苗候选疫苗,其在针对B/Victoria谱系多种亚系时表现出增强的交叉中和抗体反应。该研究采用mRNA平台,并在雌性BALB/c小鼠中测试了疫苗,结果显示D212N修饰的疫苗在针对多种流感B病毒株的挑战实验中实现了100%存活率,超过了原始的BV21毒株。研究结果表明,这种最小的抗原修饰可能在不损害其抗原完整性的前提下扩大疫苗的保护范围。未来计划在雪貂模型和人类血清中评估疫苗的性能,以进一步评估其抗原广度及预先存在的免疫对它的影响。

NRI View Point cartoon My Space Education Today Reviews Property Lifestyle E-Paper NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Telangana Dph Issues Seasonal Flu Advisory As Temperatures Set To Drop Telangana DPH issues seasonal flu advisory as temperatures set to drop The Telangana Director of Public Health has issued a seasonal flu advisory as temperatures are expected to fall by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius. The public has been urged to follow precautions, maintain hygiene and seek medical help for warning signs. By Telangana Today Published Date - 12 November 2026, 11:30 PM Representational Image Hyderabad: The Director of Public Health (DPH), Telangana on Thursday issued an advisory urging the public to take precautions against seasonal flu and spread of acute respiratory infections, as the temperatures are expected to drop by at least 2 degrees Celsius to 3 degrees Celsius in the coming days. Seasonal flu is an acute and contagious respiratory infection characterized by fever, cough, sore throat, body ache and fatigue and it spreads easily between people when they cough or sneeze, the advisory said. People with seasonal flu are advised to rest at home, drink plenty of fluids, and usually recover on their own within a week. The vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, children under 5 years, senior citizens and individuals with chronic medical conditions are at greater risk of severe illness. If they develop seasonal flu symptoms then they are advised to consult a doctor immediately, DPH, Dr Dr.B.Ravinder Nayak said. If individuals having the warning signs such as high fever, difficulty in breathing, blue colour of skin or lips, blood in sputum or altered behavior should, then they should consult the doctor immediately, he added. To Do: Cover mouth and nose with a handkerchief/tissue paper during cough or sneeze. Wash hands often with soap and water. If you have fever, cough and sneezing, avoid stay away from public places Drink plenty of water and eat nutritious food. Adequate ventilation with outdoor air is recommended in all settings to reduce the transmission Don’ts: Avoid shaking hands Avoid reuse of tissue paper or handkerchief Avoid crowded places, frequent touching of eyes, nose & mouth Avoid spitting in public places and self-medicate Join Our Whatsapp Channel Follow Us : Tags acute respiratory infections Director of Public Health Telangana seasonal flu seasonal flu symptoms Related News Telangana issues health advisory on seasonal flu amid drop in temperatures Hyderabad witnesses spurt in seasonal flu, influenza infections Coughing? Accept Diagnostic Technologies Anatomic Pathology Clinical Chemistry Digital Pathology Flow Cytometry Hematology & Serology Immunoassay Mass Spectrometry Microbiology Molecular Diagnostics Point-of-Care Urinalysis & Toxicology Lab Products Biochemicals & Chemical Reagents Information Technology Lab Automation Lab Equipment Lab Safety Labware & Consumables Quality Systems Disease States Allergy & Autoimmune Cancer Cardiovascular Cerebrovascular Dementias & Alzheimer’s Diabetes & Metabolic Diseases Infectious Diseases Kidney Disease Respiratory Disease Sepsis Womens Health Lab Management Accreditation Company News Compliance Proficiency Testing Resource Center Resources Podcasts Webcasts White Papers Videos Comparison Guides Edition Archive Select Page Diagnostic Technologies Anatomic Pathology Clinical Chemistry Digital Pathology Flow Cytometry Hematology & Serology Immunoassay Mass Spectrometry Microbiology Molecular Diagnostics Point-of-Care Urinalysis & Toxicology Lab Products Biochemicals & Chemical Reagents Information Technology Lab Automation Lab Equipment Lab Safety Labware & Consumables Quality Systems Disease States Allergy & Autoimmune Cancer Cardiovascular Cerebrovascular Dementias & Alzheimer’s Diabetes & Metabolic Diseases Infectious Diseases Kidney Disease Respiratory Disease Sepsis Womens Health Lab Management Accreditation Company News Compliance Proficiency Testing Resource Center Resources Podcasts Webcasts White Papers Videos Comparison Guides Edition Archive Flu Test Positivity Tops 10% Nationwide Nov 16, 2026 | Flu & Respiratory Infections | The CDC’s latest weekly influenza surveillance report shows activity rising across much of the US, with H1N1 continuing to dominate and hospitalizations increasing. Seasonal influenza activity is increasing in many parts of the US and is higher than typically observed at this time of year, according to the CDC’s latest weekly surveillance report for Week 44, which ended Nov 7. Clinical laboratories nationwide tested 52,287 specimens during the week, and 5,911 (11.3%) were positive for influenza. Flu test positivity rose nationally and in eight of the 10 US Department of Health and Human Services regions. It remained stable in Region 8 and declined in Region 9, which the CDC attributes to possibly incomplete reporting. Since Oct 4 (Week 40), clinical labs have tested 309,131 specimens, with 24,324 (7.9%) testing positive. Influenza A accounted for 99.2% of positive specimens in Week 44. The CDC cautioned that an earlier increase in activity does not necessarily lead to a higher seasonal peak or greater overall severity. Its preliminary in-season assessment classifies severity as low across all age groups, though the agency noted the assessment may change as activity climbs. H1N1 Predominates, With Growing Genetic Diversity Public health laboratories reported 680 positive influenza viruses in Week 44, of which 670 were influenza A and 10 were influenza B. Of the 460 influenza A viruses subtyped, 455 (98.9%) were A(H1N1)pdm09 and 5 (1.1%) were A(H3N2). Since Week 21 (the week ending May 30), 83.4% of reported influenza A viruses have been A(H1N1)pdm09, most of them in the D.3.1.1 HA subclade. The CDC noted that recently circulating D.3.1.1 viruses have divided into distinct groups with different genetic changes in their HA genes, and that there is more genetic diversity among co-circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses than previously seen. The agency said it is too early to know which viruses may predominate or whether there could be implications for vaccine effectiveness this season. Of the 764 influenza viruses genetically characterized since May 24, 555 were A(H1N1)pdm09, and 554 of those (99.8%) belonged to the D.3.1.1 subclade. Among 109 A(H3N2) viruses, 104 (95.4%) were subclade K. The 100 B/Victoria viruses were spread across several subclades, led by C.5.6.1 (48.0%) and C.3.1 (40.0%). Vaccine Match and Antiviral Susceptibility Antigenic testing showed most circulating viruses are well recognized by antisera to the 2026-2027 vaccine reference viruses. Of 147 A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses characterized by hemagglutination inhibition, 140 (95.2%) were well recognized by antisera to the A/Missouri/11/2025-like reference virus. All 35 A(H3N2) viruses and all 33 B/Victoria viruses tested were well recognized by antisera to their respective vaccine reference viruses. For antiviral susceptibility, the CDC tested 758 viruses collected since May 24 against oseltamivir, peramivir, and zanamivir, and 725 against baloxavir. Eight A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses (1.1% of all viruses tested) showed reduced inhibition by oseltamivir and carried the NA-I223V and NA-S247N substitutions. No viruses showed reduced inhibition by peramivir or zanamivir, and none showed decreased susceptibility to baloxavir. Outpatient, Hospital, and Mortality Indicators Outpatient respiratory illness is above baseline. Nationally, 3.2% of ILINet patient visits were for influenza-like illness in Week 44, above the national baseline of 2.9%. Emergency department visits with a discharge diagnosis of influenza reached 2.2%, and the percentage rose in every HHS region except Region 7, where it was stable. The CDC’s ILI activity map shows one jurisdiction at a very high level, six at a high level, and nine at a moderate level. Hospitalization data point to rising severe disease, particularly among older adults. Hospitals reported 9,584 laboratory-confirmed, influenza-associated admissions to the National Healthcare Safety Network in Week 44, a rate of 2.8 per 100,000 population. FluSurv-NET recorded 3,262 laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations between Oct. 4 and Nov. 7, for a cumulative rate of 8.7 per 100,000. The highest rate was among adults 65 and older, at 28.0 per 100,000. Influenza accounted for 0.4% of deaths in Week 44, a stable figure that has trended upward over the past eight weeks. The CDC received reports of two pediatric deaths from the current season this week, bringing the season total to five. One death from the 2025-2026 season was also reported, raising that season’s pediatric death total to 203. The CDC estimates that at least 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations, and 2,100 deaths have been associated with flu so far this season. Its FluSight forecasts predict a likely national increase in flu hospital admissions, ranging from 8,300 to 34,400, for the week ending Nov. 28. They also predict that 1.8% to 7.7% of emergency department visits will be due to flu. Novel Influenza Surveillance No new confirmed human infections with a novel influenza virus were reported to the CDC as of Nov 7. Public health laboratories have detected four H5-positive specimens since Oct 4, none of them in Week 44. The CDC noted that these figures reflect specimens tested rather than human cases. The CDC continues to recommend annual influenza vaccination for everyone 6 months and older and says prescription antivirals should be started as early as possible, especially for patients at higher risk of complications. All data are preliminary and may change as more reports are received. analysis.time: Week 44, which ended Nov 7, 2026; and since Week 21 (the week ending May 30) up to Nov 16, 2026.
